title: PRESIDENT OF INDIA UNVEILS BUST OF MAHATMA GANDHI AT THE MUSEUM OF THE CITY OF SKOPJE, NORTH MACEDONIA
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau President's Secretariat PRESIDENT OF INDIA UNVEILS BUST OF MAHATMA GANDHI AT THE MUSEUM OF THE CITY OF SKOPJE, NORTH MACEDONIA AT A TIME WHEN THE WORLD FACES CONFLICT, INTOLERANCE AND DIVISION, GANDHIJI’S FAITH IN DIALOGUE, COMPASSION AND PEACEFUL COEXISTENCE REMAINS PROFOUNDLY RELEVANT: PRESIDENT DROUPADI MURMU प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 JUL 2026 6:32PM by PIB Delhi The President of India, Smt Droupadi Murmu, along with President Gordana Siljanovska-Davkova of North Macedonia, unveiled a bust of Mahatma Gandhi at the Museum of the City of Skopje today (July 22, 2026). Addressing the gathering, the President said that Mahatma Gandhi belonged to India, but his message belongs to all humanity. She underlined that his life demonstrated that truth and non-violence are not signs of weakness, but powerful instruments for securing justice, dignity and freedom. At a time when the world faces conflict, intolerance and division, Gandhiji’s faith in dialogue, compassion and peaceful coexistence remains profoundly relevant. She said that it will inspire people to reject hatred, resolve differences peacefully and serve society with courage and empathy. The President said that this bust of Mahatma Gandhi will stand as a lasting symbol of the friendship between India and North Macedonia and of our common commitment to peace, tolerance and humanity. Among the dignitaries present on the occasion were the Mayor of the City of Skopje, Mr. Orce Gjorgjievski, members of the accompanying delegation - Minister of State for Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution, Smt Nimuben Jayantibhai Bambhaniya, and Members of Parliament Dr. Dinesh Sharma and Shri Vijay Baghel. Earlier, the President along with President Gordana Siljanovska-Davkova of North Macedonia visited Memorial of Mother Teresa in Skopje. Mother Teresa was born in Skopje where she lived until 1928. Later, she joined the Sisters of Loretto in Ireland, before moving to India. She was honoured with Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian award in 1980 for exceptional humanitarian work and selfless service. Tomorrow (July 23, 2026), the President will leave for Bucharest, Romania – the last leg of her three-nation visit. title: Vice-President inaugurates GKNM College of Nursing in Coimbatore
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Vice President's Secretariat Vice-President inaugurates GKNM College of Nursing in Coimbatore Vice-President calls for strengthening healthcare workforce to realise Viksit Bharat 2047 Compassion heals as much as medicine, says Vice-President to nursing students Ayushman Bharat transforming healthcare access for millions, says Vice-President Vice President calls for greater public awareness on organ and eye donation प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 JUL 2026 5:09PM by PIB Delhi The Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today called for strengthening India’s healthcare ecosystem through a skilled, compassionate and service-oriented workforce, saying that quality healthcare and education are the twin pillars of a healthy and developed nation. He said the country’s journey towards Viksit Bharat by 2047 would require collective efforts to improve healthcare delivery, promote preventive healthcare and nurture dedicated healthcare professionals. Vice President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan inaugurated the GKNM college of Nursing in Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu today. Emphasising the vital role of nurses, the Vice President said they are far more than caregivers - they instill confidence, comfort and hope in patients, with their… pic.twitter.com/dGWcWVDx1N — Vice-President of India (@VPIndia) July 22, 2026 Addressing the gathering after inaugurating the GKNM Group College of Nursing in Coimbatore, the Vice-President described the institution as another milestone in the long tradition of public service rendered by the GKNM Group. He commended the G. Kuppuswamy Naidu Charitable Trust for its remarkable contribution to healthcare and education over the past several decades, noting that its 50-bed hospital established in 1952 has today grown into a 750-bed multi-specialty institution while simultaneously expanding its educational initiatives from schools to higher education. Emphasising the importance of the nursing profession, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said nurses are far more than caregivers. “They make patients feel safe, secure and cared for. Along with medicines, their compassion and concern play an indispensable role in healing,” he said. He urged students entering the profession to carry out their responsibilities with self-confidence, compassion, dedication and courage, and always uphold the nobility of their calling. Highlighting the transformation taking place in India’s healthcare sector, the Vice-President said the Ayushman Bharat programme has earned global recognition for expanding access to quality healthcare. He noted that nearly 44 crore people have received health insurance coverage of up to ₹5 lakh under the Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana. Referring to healthcare initiatives for senior citizens, he said free healthcare under the Pradhan Mantri Vaya Vandana Yojana and the ongoing digitisation of health services are making quality healthcare more accessible across the country. The Vice-President stressed the importance of preventive healthcare and called for concerted efforts to eliminate anaemia among women and children, ensure healthier pregnancies and improve nutrition from infancy through adolescence. He also appealed for greater public awareness about organ and eye donation, describing them as noble acts that save lives and restore hope. Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said the GKNM Group embodies these ideals through its unwavering commitment to healthcare and education, and expressed confidence that the newly inaugurated College of Nursing would produce competent and compassionate healthcare professionals who would contribute significantly to nation-building. The Vice-President congratulated the trustees, management, faculty, nurses, students and staff of the GKNM Group and wished the institution continued success in its mission of serving society through excellence in healthcare and education. He also expressed hope that the G. Kuppuswamy Naidu Charitable Trust would soon establish a medical college that would produce skilled medical professionals with a spirit of service, committed to caring for the poorest and most vulnerable. Governor of Tamil Nadu Shri Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar; President, Kuppuswamy Naidu Charity Trust for Education and Medical Relief Shri R. Gopinath; and other dignitaries were present during the occasion *** PR/ASM/VM (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2287768) आगंतुक पटल  : 194 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Tamil Vice President's Secretariat Vice-President inaugurates GKNM College of Nursing in Coimbatore Vice-President calls for strengthening healthcare workforce to realise Viksit Bharat 2047 Compassion heals as much as medicine, says Vice-President to nursing students Ayushman Bharat transforming healthcare access for millions, says Vice-President Vice President calls for greater public awareness on organ and eye donation प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: PM Chairs High-Level Meeting of Secretaries to Review Progress of Rural Development, Agriculture, Social Welfare and Allied Sectors towards Viksit Bharat Goals
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Prime Minister's Office PM Chairs High-Level Meeting of Secretaries to Review Progress of Rural Development, Agriculture, Social Welfare and Allied Sectors towards Viksit Bharat Goals PM emphasises that the welfare of citizens must remain at the heart of all reforms PM Stresses the Need to Evolve Governance Processes in Line with Changing Times PM Calls for a Whole-of-Government Approach and breaking silos to achieve the nation's development goals PM says that dream to build a Viksit Bharat should become a Jan Andolan and Youth should be it’s foundation PM underscores the Need for Coordinated Action to Combat Drug Abuse and Empower Youth PM Stresses Integrated Approach to Position India as a Global Sports Hub PM Highlights Transformative Potential of PM-KUSUM and Need for Global Skill Mapping Secretaries share their experiences and perspectives on various initiatives and challenges in their respective domains प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 JUL 2026 7:37PM by PIB Delhi Prime Minister today chaired a high-level meeting with Secretaries to review progress of rural development, agriculture, social welfare and allied sectors towards Viksit Bharat Goals, at his residence at 7, Lok Kalyan Marg earlier today. Prime Minister emphasised that the welfare of citizens must remain at the heart of all reforms. He said that reforms designed around people's needs should gather real momentum and deliver meaningful transformation. He emphasised that the objective of reforms is not merely to improve the functioning of the Government, but to accelerate India's journey towards becoming a developed nation. Prime Minister highlighted that governance systems are witnessing rapid changes and stressed the importance of adapting and strengthening governance processes to effectively meet the needs of a dynamic and evolving environment. He suggested undertaking a comprehensive mapping of emerging requirements across various Ministries and Departments. Prime Minister stressed the need for a whole-of-government approach to achieve the nation's development goals. He further emphasised that the dream to build a Viksit Bharat should become a Jan Andolan and that India's youth should form the foundation of this vision. Prime Minister underscored the importance of tackling the serious issue of drug abuse among youth. He suggested that efforts should be made to develop an institutional mechanism to break departmental silos and foster greater inter-departmental coordination and convergence in youth-centric initiatives. Prime Minister further emphasized the need to adopt an integrated approach for the development of sports. He noted that, with sports tourism emerging as a key focus area, India should aspire to host major international sporting events to establish itself as a global sports hub. He stressed the importance of promoting technology and fostering innovation through startups in the sports sector. Prime Minister highlighted that the widespread adoption of initiatives such as the PM KUSUM Scheme by farmers can bring transformative changes to the agriculture sector. He further stressed the need for a global mapping of skill requirements to ensure better alignment with international opportunities and future needs. The Secretaries shared their experiences and perspectives on various initiatives and challenges in their respective domains. The Prime Minister shared his suggestions and his vision for the future course of action. The meeting was marked by comprehensive and productive discussions across the sectors, focusing on effective implementation, greater convergence and accelerated progress towards the goals of Viksit Bharat. The meeting was attended by the Cabinet Secretary, Secretaries of key Ministries as well as senior officials from the Prime Minister's Office. **** MJPS/SS/PRK (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2287957) आगंतुक पटल  : 301 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: हिन्दी , Gujarati Prime Minister's Office PM Chairs High-Level Meeting of Secretaries to Review Progress of Rural Development, Agriculture, Social Welfare and Allied Sectors towards Viksit Bharat Goals PM emphasises that the welfare of citizens must remain at the heart of all reforms PM Stresses the Need to Evolve Governance Processes in Line with Changing Times PM Calls for a Whole-of-Government Approach and breaking silos to achieve the nation's development goals PM says that dream to build a Viksit Bharat should become a Jan Andolan and Youth should be it’s foundation PM underscores the Need for Coordinated Action to Combat Drug Abuse and Empower Youth PM Stresses Integrated Approach to Position India as a Global Sports Hub PM Highlights Transformative Potential of PM-KUSUM and Need for Global Skill Mapping Secretaries share their experiences and perspectives on various initiatives and challenges in their respective domains प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Union Minister Shri Prataprao Jadhav Inaugurated Prakriti Café at Ayush Bhawan
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau AYUSH Union Minister Shri Prataprao Jadhav Inaugurated Prakriti Café at Ayush Bhawan "Prakriti Café” Reflects Our Vision of Promoting Wellness Through Healthy Everyday Choices: Shri Prataprao Jadhav Prakriti Café Initiative Promotes Ayush-Inspired Healthy Eating at the Workplace प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 JUL 2026 4:28PM by PIB Delhi Shri Prataprao Jadhav, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge), Ministry of Ayush and Minister of State for Health & Family Welfare, today inaugurated Prakriti Café at Ayush Bhawan, a first-of-its-kind workplace initiative of the Ministry of Ayush aimed at promoting healthy dietary practices inspired by Ayush Ahaar. Highlighting the significance of the initiative, Union Minister Shri Prataprao Jadhav, said, “Prakriti Café is a reflection of our vision of promoting wellness not only through healthcare, but also through healthy everyday choices. Food is an integral part of our overall well-being, and nutritious food in itself can be a form of nourishment and support for good health. Through initiatives such as Ayush Ahaar, we seek to encourage greater awareness about nutritious, wholesome and balanced eating. Shri Jadhav also noted that today, our dietary habits are changing, and the growing culture of junk food is adversely affecting health and contributing to lifestyle-related diseases. We must recognise the risks associated with such unhealthy habits, particularly among young people, and encourage healthier choices. Prakriti Café will provide a space where people can experience the values of healthy living in their daily lives, with wholesome Ayush-inspired food available at affordable prices.” Emphasising the importance of mindful nutrition as part of a healthy lifestyle, Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha, Secretary, Ministry of Ayush, said, “The idea behind Prakriti Café is to bring the principles of Ayush closer to everyday life. A healthy lifestyle is built through simple and consistent choices, and mindful eating is an important part of that journey. We hope Prakriti Café will become a space that encourages healthy food habits, community, and a greater appreciation of India’s rich traditions of wholesome nutrition.” The café offers a range of fresh and wholesome food options inspired by the Ayush Ahaar initiative, which seeks to promote nutritious dietary practices rooted in India’s traditional knowledge systems. The initiative also aims to create greater awareness about the importance of food and nutrition in supporting a healthy and balanced lifestyle. The menu features a variety of nutritious preparations, including beetroot and oats cutlet, kosambari, millet dhokla, khandvi, oats poha, little millet vegetable upma and makhana kheer prepared with jaggery, along with refreshing options such as coconut water and herbal beverages including tulsi-ginger tea and green tea. The offerings reflect the principles of Ayush Ahaar by encouraging balanced, wholesome and nutritious food choices in everyday life. The inauguration ceremony was attended by senior officials and employees of the Ministry of Ayush. The launch of Prakriti Café marks another step in the Ministry's efforts to foster a workplace culture that promotes health, wellness, and mindful living by integrating the principles of Ayush with contemporary approaches to preventive healthcare. *** SR/SV/SG (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2287721) आगंतुक पटल  : 236 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu AYUSH Union Minister Shri Prataprao Jadhav Inaugurated Prakriti Café at Ayush Bhawan "Prakriti Café” Reflects Our Vision of Promoting Wellness Through Healthy Everyday Choices: Shri Prataprao Jadhav Prakriti Café Initiative Promotes Ayush-Inspired Healthy Eating at the Workplace प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: ICAR-CISH–APEDA Sea Route Protocol Enables Successful Export of 12.5 Tonnes of Dashehari and Langra Mangoes to Dubai
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Agriculture &
Farmers Welfare ICAR-CISH–APEDA Sea Route Protocol Enables Successful Export of 12.5 Tonnes of Dashehari and Langra Mangoes to Dubai प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 JUL 2026 6:58PM by PIB Delhi In a major breakthrough for India's fresh mango export sector, 12.5 tonnes of premium Dashehari and Langra mangoes have been successfully exported from Amroha, Uttar Pradesh, to Dubai, United Arab Emirates, through a 40-foot reefer container by sea using the sea route export protocol jointly developed by ICAR–Central Institute for Subtropical Horticulture (ICAR-CISH), Lucknow, and the Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA). The consignment was exported by Shehnaz Export, Amroha, in association with Attashi Global, to Lulu Group, UAE, one of the leading retail chains in the Gulf region, with technical guidance from ICAR-CISH and support from APEDA. The mangoes were harvested on 22 nd June, 2026 and handled in accordance with the recommended scientific post-harvest management practices. The fruits were treated with METWASH developed by ICAR-CISH for extension of shelf life, scientifically graded, packed at the Amroha Pack House, loaded into a 40-foot reefer container, and transported to Dubai by sea under a continuous cold chain. Owing to Western Disturbance-related delays, the consignment reached the destination market on 17 th July 2026, completing a 25-day harvest-to-market transit period. Despite the extended transit time, nearly 90% of the mangoes were found to be in good marketable condition upon arrival, demonstrating the effectiveness of the technology. The successful validation of the sea-route protocol thus provides a sustainable pathway for increasing farmers' income through cost-effective exports. Since sea freight is substantially more economical than air freight, exporters were able to offer higher procurement prices to farmers. As a result, mango growers realized an additional income of approximately ₹15–20 per kg over conventional export channels, significantly enhancing farm profitability while maintaining the competitiveness of Indian mangoes in international markets. This is the first successful commercial sea shipment of Dashehari and Langra mangoes from Uttar Pradesh to Dubai under such an extended 25-day harvest-to-market transit period, demonstrating that premium Indian mangoes can now be exported economically through sea freight without compromising quality. The achievement is expected to encourage exporters to increasingly adopt sea freight, thereby expanding India's fresh mango exports to the Gulf region and other international markets. The technology is expected to accelerate the commercialization of sea-route exports of mangoes from Uttar Pradesh and other mango-producing states, opening new opportunities in the Gulf and other international markets while enhancing export earnings, reducing logistics costs, and improving the livelihoods of mango growers of Uttar Pradesh. * **** RC/MS (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2287909) आगंतुक पटल  : 122 Ministry of Agriculture &

The technology is expected to accelerate the commercialization of sea-route exports of mangoes from Uttar Pradesh and other mango-producing states, opening new opportunities in the Gulf and other international markets while enhancing export earnings, reducing logistics costs, and improving the livelihoods of mango growers of Uttar Pradesh. * **** RC/MS (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2287909)

title: Big initiative by Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan to provide relief to Totapuri mango farmers of Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Agriculture &
Farmers Welfare Big initiative by Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan to provide relief to Totapuri mango farmers of Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka A high-level committee formed by Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan presents a report on farmers’ complaints A committee formed on instructions of Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh visits fields, mandis and factories to assess ground situation Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh conducts in-depth review of expert committee report during the important meeting in Delhi “Recommendation to make 22-25% real pulp mandatory in mango-based drinks in interest of farmers and consumers”: Shri Shivraj Singh “Major plan to improve horticulture through new and top-working varieties in Totapuri orchards”: Shri Shivraj Singh Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh stresses zonal purchase, fruit bags and FPO-based processing for farmers “Centre, states, ICAR and APEDA will together give new direction to Totapuri value chain”: Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 JUL 2026 6:26PM by PIB Delhi Amid continuous complaints of falling incomes of farmers producing Totapuri mangoes in Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka, and falling prices in mandis, Union Minister for Agriculture and Farmers’ Welfare, and Rural Development, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan has issued comprehensive directives for wide-ranging improvements in the cultivation, processing and marketing system of Totapuri mangoes after detailed discussions on the recommendations of a high-level committee constituted by him. Union Agriculture Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan today held a high-level review meeting at Krishi Bhavan, New Delhi, to assess the problems faced by Totapuri mango-producing farmers of Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka, and took important decisions to strengthen the entire value chain of Totapuri mangoes based on the report of a high-level expert committee. The committee visited fields, mandis and pulp-making units and presented the ground conditions, on the basis of which Union Minister Shri Chouhan made it clear that the file will not simply be closed after preparing a report, but concrete steps will be taken at all three levels – policy, technology and market. Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan chaired the high-level meeting to review the problems of Totapuri mango-producing farmers of Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka, which was attended by all senior officials including Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) Director General Dr. M.L. Jat. The committee chairman, Director of ICAR–CISH (Central Institute for Subtropical Horticulture, Lucknow), Dr. Damodaran T., presented the report. This meeting was focused on the report of the expert committee constituted under the Indian Council of Agricultural Research to examine issues related to decline in cultivation and prices of Totapuri mangoes and to suggest solutions. The committee was constituted under an order dated 2 July 2026, which included scientists from ICAR–CISH (Central Institute for Subtropical Horticulture, Lucknow), ICAR–IIHR (Indian Institute of Horticultural Research, Bengaluru), ICAR–CISH, experts from Dr. YSR Horticultural University, Andhra Pradesh, and officials from the State Horticulture Department. On the directions of Union Minister Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan, the committee conducted field visits from July 8 to 10 in the Tirupati and Chittoor districts of Andhra Pradesh, where it met farmers, Farmer Producer Organisations (FPOs), mandi representatives, pulp-making units, exporters and the district administration, and reviewed all stages of the Totapuri mango value chain. Presenting its report in the meeting, the committee stated that the major reasons behind the decline in Totapuri mango prices this year include lack of timely coordination in processing capacity and procurement arrangements, low quantity of real pulp in mango-based beverages in the domestic market, and fluctuations in the global market. The committee also highlighted that in many places, factories are unable to make timely purchases at the beginning of the season, while farmers’ produce reaches mandis and processing units simultaneously, causing sudden price crashes and leaving farmers at a loss. On the issue of mango-based beverages, the committee suggested that all such products should be made to contain 22-25 per cent of real natural mango pulp. In the committee’s view, if only those beverages which contain more than the prescribed limit of pulp are kept in the 5 per cent concessional Goods and Services Tax (GST) category, and higher GST rates are applied to low-pulp products, then on the one hand consumption of Totapuri mango pulp will increase, and on the other hand consumers will get more nutritious and genuine fruit-based beverages. Considering this proposal, Union Minister Shri Chouhan directed the convening of an inter-ministerial meeting among the relevant Ministries – Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI), GST Council, Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Food Processing Industries, Ministry of Agriculture and Ministry of Health – so that consensus can be reached on necessary standards and tax structure. To stabilise and systematise the Totapuri mango value chain, the committee recommended the constitution of a Central Coordination and Price Stabilisation Committee, which will function as an apex institutional mechanism for major producing States such as Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka. Before every mango season, this committee will review crop estimates, processing and export demand, agricultural costs and market conditions, and will help in determining indicative profitable farm-gate procurement prices for farmers and reference prices for mango pulp, so that clear signals are available in advance to both farmers and the industry. It was also informed in the meeting that a large area of Totapuri mango cultivation in the Chittoor, Tirupati, Annamayya and Kadapa districts of Andhra Pradesh consists of old orchards whose productivity and quality have both declined. To deal with this situation, the committee recommended rejuvenation of orchards through the top-working technique, under which scions of high-value varieties such as Neelam, Alphonso, Himayat, Banganapalli and others can be grafted onto existing trees, and a new, more valuable crop can be obtained in two to three years. Along with this, emphasis was also laid on implementing Good Agricultural Practices (GAP) at the cluster level and providing training, demonstration gardens and technical assistance to farmers. To improve fruit quality and increase access to premium domestic markets, the committee suggested that fruit bags (fruit covers) be provided in the initial phase in an area of about 23,333 hectares in the Chittoor, Tirupati, Annamayya and Kadapa districts, so that the external texture of the fruit remains better, pest damage is reduced, and Totapuri mangoes can reach higher-priced mandis. Along with this, it was recommended to develop zonal procurement and initial processing arrangements, under which the Horticulture Department, processing industry and Farmer Producer Organizations will jointly prepare an annual procurement plan. It was also recommended for the Andhra Pradesh Government that it should issue a Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) making it mandatory for all registered processing units to begin procurement and pulp production from May 15 every year. During the meeting, there was also discussion on farmer-led processing units and FPO (Farmer Producer Organisation)-based value addition models. Using technologies developed by ICAR–CISH and IIHR, emphasis was laid on the possibilities of making ‘mango butter’ and other value-added products from the seed kernel of mangoes, so that Totapuri mango seeds and by-products can also become a source of additional income for farmers. In the meeting, Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA) representatives informed about efforts to expand domestic and international markets for Totapuri and other Indian mangoes, especially through sea routes to reduce costs and increase access to new destinations. In this context, Shri Shivraj Chouhan said that an integrated export and marketing strategy will be prepared for Totapuri-based processed products and fresh table mangoes with the cooperation of APEDA, ICAR and State Governments. During the meeting, Shri Shivraj Singh Chouhan made it clear that the Central Government wants to make the entire Totapuri mango value chain farmer-centric. He said that the Central and State Governments, ICAR, APEDA, Farmer Producer Organisations and the processing industry will all share responsibility, and a clear roadmap will be prepared by coordinating GST, food safety standards and State policies. He expressed confidence that if the suggested measures are implemented in a comprehensive manner, there will be a permanent increase in the income of Totapuri mango-producing farmers in Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka, and Indian mangoes will be able to establish an even stronger identity in the global market. * **** RC/MS/MK (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2287885) आगंतुक पटल  : 172 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: हिन्दी , Gujarati Ministry of Agriculture &

title: Bharat 6G Alliance and Spectrum Roadmap for 6G in India
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Communications Bharat 6G Alliance and Spectrum Roadmap for 6G in India प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 JUL 2026 6:03PM by PIB Delhi The Bharat 6G Alliance (B6GA), an industry and academia-led society, has expanded to become a 90 member organisation as of 15 th July 2026. These members represent a broad and diverse ecosystem comprising telecom service providers, telecom equipment manufacturers, startups, research and development institutions, academia and other stakeholders from the telecom sector. B6GA has constituted seven working groups covering key domains such as 6G technologies, spectrum, applications, use cases and revenue streams, devices and components, green and sustainability aspects and outreach. The Alliance serves as a collaborative platform for industry, academia, startups and research institutions to strengthen the domestic research, innovation and IPR ecosystem through industry-academia engagement, identification of technology gaps, and development of proposals for testbeds and advanced research aligned with India's 6G Vision. The spectrum working group, one of the seven working groups constituted under the Bharat 6G Alliance, has submitted a report titled "Spectrum Roadmap for 6G in India”. Separately, the Department of Telecommunications, after consultation with stakeholders including the Bharat 6G Alliance, has released the Spectrum Roadmap for 6G services, which can be accessed online at https://www.dot.gov.in/static/uploads/2026/02/092d793d6ea912a5dd79bf0c26ea1a84.pdf . A three-year project has been approved from the Telecom Technology Development Fund under Digital Bharat Nidhi for the establishment of a 6G Terahertz testbed at Society for Applied Microwave Electronics Engineering & Research (SAMEER), Kolkata, an autonomous research and development body under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology along with three consortium members, namely, Indian Institute of Technology Madras, Indian Institute of Technology Guwahati, and Indian Institute of Technology Patna. Under this project, a high data rate line of sight link was demonstrated in the India Mobile Congress (IMC) 2025. India has contributed in the International Telecommunications Union (ITU) under the International Mobile Technology (IMT) 2030 framework, also called 6G by industry for inclusion of “ubiquitous connectivity” as one of the six usage scenarios of 6G and coverage, interoperability and sustainability as capabilities of 6G technology. Further, to strengthen India's global leadership in 6G, the Government is also supporting active participation of Indian stakeholders in international standardisation bodies such as 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP), ITU and oneM2M through initiatives under the Department of Telecommunications’ Technology Development and Investment Promotion (TDIP) scheme which provides financial assistance for membership fees, participation in international standardisation meetings, hosting of such meetings in India, pilot testing and validation of telecom products. The TDIP scheme covers eligible startups and MSMEs across the country. This information was given by the Union Minister of State for Communications and Rural Development Dr. Chandra Sekhar Pemmasani in a written reply to a question in the Lok Sabha today . ***** NJ/AR (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2287851) आगंतुक पटल  : 290 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Telugu Ministry of Communications Bharat 6G Alliance and Spectrum Roadmap for 6G in India प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Branch of the Bharatiya Beej Sahakari Samiti Limited in Bihar
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Cooperation Branch of the Bharatiya Beej Sahakari Samiti Limited in Bihar प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 JUL 2026 5:38PM by PIB Delhi No formal branch office of Bharatiya Beej Sahakari Samiti Limited (BBSSL) has presently been established in Bihar. However, BBSSL has an operational presence in the State through its field official, who coordinates seed distribution, business development and monitoring of seed-related activities. BBSSL is undertaking seed business in Bihar through the Bihar Rajya Beej Nigam Limited, which is the designated nodal agency for BBSSL in the State. Seed production and distribution activities are coordinated with the nodal agency, local cooperative institutions and other stakeholders. During the financial year 2026–27, BBSSL has also supplied various crop seeds directly to 20 cooperative societies in Bihar, thereby strengthening its cooperative-based distribution network in the State. BBSSL follows a farmer-centric pricing model under which seed-producing farmers are paid the highest of: (i) MSP plus a minimum 10 per cent incentive on graded seed, or (ii) the prevailing mandi market price, or (iii) the concerned State Seed Corporation’s procurement rate. This ensures assured procurement, protects farmers from price fluctuations and provides them a remunerative premium for meeting the higher quality and technical requirements of seed production . This information was given by Union Minister for Home and Cooperation Shri Amit Shah in a written reply in Rajya Sabha. ***** AK/AP (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2287817) आगंतुक पटल  : 104 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: हिन्दी Ministry of Cooperation Branch of the Bharatiya Beej Sahakari Samiti Limited in Bihar प्रविष्टि तिथि:

content:

title: Strengthening of cooperative societies in Odisha
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Cooperation Strengthening of cooperative societies in Odisha प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 JUL 2026 5:34PM by PIB Delhi As per the National Cooperative Database (NCD), as on 15.07.2026, there are a total of 8,667 cooperative societies in Odisha, out of which 8,063 cooperative societies are functional. To strengthen cooperative societies, the Government launched the Central Sector project for Computerization of PACS, in 2022. Initially, 63,000 PACS were approved under the project with a total financial outlay of ₹2,516 crore. The project has now been expanded to cover 79,630 PACS with a revised financial outlay of ₹2,925.39 crore. It aims to bring all functional PACS onto a common ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning) based national software. The project also links PACS with NABARD through State Cooperative Banks (StCBs) and District Central Cooperative Banks (DCCBs). Odisha joined the project in 2025. A total of 4,240 PACS have been sanctioned under the PACS computerization project in Odisha. Under the project, financial assistance of ₹25.07 crore has been provided to Odisha. This includes ₹18.07 crore during FY 2025–26 and ₹7.00 crore during FY 2026–27. Additionally, as on 30.06.2026, the National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC) has cumulatively disbursed ₹3,352.03 crore for the development of the cooperative sector in Odisha. The year-wise details of the amount disbursed during the last five years are given at Annexure-1. The Ministry of Cooperation, since its inception on 06.07.2021, has undertaken several initiatives to realize the vision of “Sahakar-se-Samriddhi” and to enhance the cooperative growth across the country including Odisha. Key areas of initiatives include: Making Primary Cooperatives economically vibrant and transparent; Strengthening the Urban and Rural Cooperative Banks; Relief to Cooperative Societies in the Income Tax Act; Revival of Cooperative Sugar Mills; Three new National Level Multi-State Societies; Capacity Building in Cooperatives; Use of Information Technology for ‘Ease of Doing Business’; Creation of National Cooperative Database (NCD); National Cooperation Policy (NCP); Establishment of Tribhuvan Sahkari University Other Initiatives The Ministry of Cooperation has taken proactive measures to convert Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS), Dairy, and Fisheries Cooperatives into Multipurpose cooperative societies. This initiative aims to enhance business diversification, strengthen financial sustainability, and prevent closures by enabling cooperatives to engage in a wider range of economic activities. The NCD is used for identification of gaps in the geographical spread of cooperatives, thereby supporting the formation of new multipurpose PACS/dairy/fisheries cooperative societies. It also enables the development of the Cooperative Ranking Framework to promote healthy competition. title: Status of Bharat Taxi
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Cooperation Status of Bharat Taxi प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 JUL 2026 5:33PM by PIB Delhi Sahakar Taxi Cooperative Limited (STCL), registered under the Multi-State Cooperative Societies Act, 2002, was established on 6 June 2025 by eight national-level cooperative institutions and was officially launched on 5 February 2026 under the aegis of the Ministry of Cooperation. STCL has introduced a cooperative-based mobility ecosystem that represents a paradigm shift from the conventional “driver-partner” model to the “Sarathi-owner” model, under which drivers become members and owners of the cooperative society, participate in its governance through representation on the Board of Management, and share in the cooperative's surplus. Through its Bharat Taxi platform, STCL operates on a zero-commission model, enabling drivers to retain their earnings while the cooperative's surplus is distributed among its Sarathi-members. The platform integrates cooperative ownership with technology-enabled ride-hailing services, including transparent fare structures, real-time vehicle tracking, multilingual mobile interfaces, and round-the-clock customer support, providing a homegrown and indigenous alternative to investment-driven aggregator platforms. The implementation of Bharat Taxi Services is being carried out in a phased manner across the country. The Bharat Taxi platform, comprising the Sarathi (driver) application, passenger application and the backend management system, has been developed and is being expanded in a phased manner. The rollout in individual cities and States is contingent on factors such as operational preparedness, availability of Sarathis, completion of statutory requirements, and coordination with the concerned State Governments, cooperative institutions and other stakeholders. The implementation includes registration and onboarding of Sarathis, customer enrolment, training programmes and expansion of services to identified cities and States. 7.76 lakh Sarathis (drivers) have been registered on the Bharat Taxi platform and their document verification has been completed. 40.84 lakh customers have been registered on the platform. Presently the Bharat Taxi is operational in cities of Delhi-NCR and Gujrat. Bharat Taxi and Yatri Sathi are separate mobility platforms operating under different institutional arrangements. Bharat Taxi is a cooperative-based mobility platform operated by STCL under the provisions of the Multi-State Cooperative Societies Act, 2002. Yatri Sathi is a State Government initiative developed, owned and operated by the Department of Information Technology and Electronics (DITE), Government of West Bengal for providing taxi aggregation services within the State. This information was given by Union Minister for Home and Cooperation Shri Amit Shah in a written reply in Rajya Sabha. ***** AK/AP (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2287804) आगंतुक पटल  : 154 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी Ministry of Cooperation Status of Bharat Taxi प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Promotion of AI and digital platforms in cooperatives
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Cooperation Promotion of AI and digital platforms in cooperatives प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 JUL 2026 5:29PM by PIB Delhi AI and digital platforms are getting progressively promoted across cooperative training institutions through academic, training and institutional initiatives. Technology-driven teaching pedagogy and learning platforms are being adopted by cooperative training institutions such as RICM, Chandigarh in Punjab. The measures include use of smart classrooms with interactive digital boards, projectors and ICT-enabled teaching tools; adoption of blended learning through e-content, online classes and Learning Management Systems (LMS); and training of faculty in ICT tools and digital pedagogy. Digital learning initiatives are also reviewed periodically for their effective utilisation. Capacity building for teachers and cooperative professionals is being supported through Faculty Development Programmes (FDPs), refresher courses, seminars, workshops, webinars and other professional development programmes. The programmes cover areas such as cooperative management, banking and finance, governance, digital banking, digital transformation and other emerging areas of the cooperative sector. title: ‘Heritage Artisan Cooperatives’
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Cooperation ‘Heritage Artisan Cooperatives’ प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 JUL 2026 5:25PM by PIB Delhi Based on the information received from the State of Odisha, Directorate of Handicrafts under the administrative control of Handlooms, Textiles & Handicrafts Department, Odisha, the functioning of Handicraft Cooperative Societies (HCSs) of Odisha including the HCSs of Puri district is supervised time to time. An integrated RCS digital portal has been launched in Odisha. As per the National Cooperative Database (NCD), there are a total of 756 registered cooperative societies in the Puri district. The National Cooperative Development Corporation (NCDC) implements sector-specific schemes and focused financial products aligned with the evolving needs of the cooperative sector, including artisan cooperative societies across the country, including those in the Puri district of Odisha. Details of the Schemes of NCDC are enclosed at Annexure A. The key measures undertaken to support and strengthen this artisan cooperatives are as under: Financial Assistance for Infrastructure & Marketing: NCDC provides financial assistance to eligible artisan cooperatives for infrastructure creation, value addition, processing, and marketing of artisan and handicraft products. Capacity Building & Entrepreneurship: Various training and awareness programmes are regularly conducted for artisans to facilitate entrepreneurship development, marketing support, and to improve their access to institutional finance. Promotion of Digital Literacy: To facilitate digital onboarding and modern business practices, digital literacy is integrated as an essential component of all training and capacity-building interventions. These promotional and financial assistance schemes are available to all eligible artisan cooperative societies across the country, including Puri, subject to the fulfilment of the prescribed guidelines and eligibility criteria under the respective schemes. These provide opportunity to address and overcome, challenges. As on 30.06.2026, NCDC has disbursed ₹ 3,352.03 crore for cooperative development in Odisha State. The details of disbursement during last five years in the State is provided at Annexure-B . As on 30.06.2026, NCDC has disbursed ₹3.78 Cr in Puri district during the last five years (since 01.04.2021). There are 17 HCSs functional in Puri district which are engaged in different handicrafts. Other artisans are sensitized on digital literacy and consolidation of required documents for their onboarding into e-commerce platforms through different training programmes and awareness camps.   Marketing assistance to handicraft artisans/ members of Handicrafts Cooperative Societies is provided through exhibitions/ fairs/ melas organized at District level/ State level and National level. ****** Annexure-A SCHEMES / ACTIVITIES ASSISTED BY NCDC 1) CORPORATION SPONSORED SCHEMES: A)  ACTIVITIES ASSISTED: NCDC provides financial assistance in the form of loans (both Term Loans and Investment Loans) and subsidy to the cooperative societies for their development. The loa n component is provided from out of NCDC’s own funds while the eligible subsidy is provided after dovetailing from other Central Sector Schemes. The list of activities assisted by NCDC is as under: - Marketing: Processing: Storage: Cold Chain: Industrial: Distribution of essential consumer articles through cooperatives: Credit & Service Cooperatives/ Notified Services: Cooperative Banking Unit: Agricultural Services: District Plan Schemes: Weaker Section Cooperatives: Assistance for Computerization of Cooperatives: Promotional and Developmental programs. B.   FOCUSSED PRODUCTS OF NCDC: YUVA SAHAKAR - ­Cooperative Enterprise Support and Innovation Scheme: The scheme launched in the financial year 2019-20 aims at encouraging newly formed cooperative societies with new and/ or innovative ideas. Ayushman Sahakar: The scheme launched in the financial year 2020-21 has a comprehensive approach to cover hospitals, healthcare, medical education, nursing education, paramedical education, health insurance and holistic health systems such as AYUSH. NAndini Sahakar: The scheme is in operation since financial year 2020-21, which aims to improve the socio-economic status of women and supports the entrepreneurial dynamism of women through women’s cooperatives. It converges critical inputs of women’s enterprise, business plan formulation, capacity development, credit and subsidy, and/ or interest subvention of other schemes. DAIRY SAHAKAR: The scheme launched in the financial year 2021-22 is a cooperative dairy business focused framework of financial assistance for encouraging cooperatives to achieve higher outcomes in ESG (environmental, social, governance) linked activities. It includes the creation of infrastructure by cooperatives for new projects and modernization and/or expansion of existing projects. DIGITAL SAHAKAR: The scheme is in operation since 2021-22 aligned with the principles of Digital India, NCDC has conceived a focused financial assistance framework for Digitally Empowered Cooperatives for handholding and credit linkage by NCDC, dovetailed with grant, subsidy, incentives, etc. from the Government of India / State / UT / agencies with the objective of cooperatives actively partaking in Digital India. SWAYAM SHAKTI SAHAKAR YOJNA: The scheme launched in the financial year 2022-23 for providing NCDC's financial assistance to Agricultural Credit Cooperatives for providing loan/advances to Women Self Help Groups (SHGs) . DEERGHAVADHI KRISHAK PUNJI SAHAKAR YOJNA: The scheme launched in the financial year 2022-23 for extending NCDC's long-term financial assistance to Agricultural Credit Cooperatives towards their onward lending of long-term loans/advances for activities/commodities/services under the purview of NCDC . SAHAKAR INNOVATION SCHEME: The scheme was launched in the financial year 2025-26 to provide grant assistance of up to ₹25 lakh to eligible cooperative societies for promoting innovation, adoption of new technologies, development of innovative products, services and business models, market linkages, and sustainability-oriented initiatives, thereby strengthening the cooperative sector and supporting emerging cooperatives with innovative and scalable ideas. II    Other Central Schemes: Agricultural Marketing Infrastructure (AMI) sub scheme of Central Sector Integrated Scheme on Agriculture Marketing (CSISAM) for Storage and other than Storage Infrastructure -DAC&FW, MOA&FW Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (Training) - DAC&FW, MOA&FW Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH) - DAC&FW, MOA&FW Interest Subvention & Credit Guarantee through Financing Facility under Agriculture Infrastructure Fund scheme - Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers’ Welfare. Assistance for Boosting Seed Production component under Sub-Mission for Seed and Planting Material (SMSP) of National Mission on Agricultural Extension and Technology (NMAET) PM Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY) – Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying PM Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah-Yojana (PM-MKSSY) – sub scheme under PMMSY by Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying. PM Formalization of Micro Food Processing Enterprises (PMFME )- Ministry of Food Processing Industries Scheme for Formation and Promotion of 10,000 Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs) – Ministry of Agriculture & Farmer’s Welfare. (i) Pradhan Mantri Kisan Sampada Yojna (PMKSY) – Scheme for Food Processing and Value Addition - Ministry of Food Processing Industries. (ii) Pradhan Mantri Kisan Sampada Yojna (PMKSY) - Integrated Cold Chain and Value Addition Infrastructure Scheme - Ministry of Food Processing Industries. National Scheduled Tribes Finance and Development Corporation (NSTFDC) - Ministry of Tribal Affairs. National Livestock Mission (NLM) and Rashtriya Gokul Mission (RGM) - Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying. Re-aligned Animal Husbandry Infrastructure Development Fund (AHIDF), Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying. **** Annexure-B Last 5 Years Activity wise Disbursement in Odisha (Rs.in crore) S. NAndini Sahakar: The scheme is in operation since financial year 2020-21, which aims to improve the socio-economic status of women and supports the entrepreneurial dynamism of women through women’s cooperatives. It converges critical inputs of women’s enterprise, business plan formulation, capacity development, credit and subsidy, and/ or interest subvention of other schemes. DAIRY SAHAKAR: The scheme launched in the financial year 2021-22 is a cooperative dairy business focused framework of financial assistance for encouraging cooperatives to achieve higher outcomes in ESG (environmental, social, governance) linked activities. It includes the creation of infrastructure by cooperatives for new projects and modernization and/or expansion of existing projects. DIGITAL SAHAKAR: The scheme is in operation since 2021-22 aligned with the principles of Digital India, NCDC has conceived a focused financial assistance framework for Digitally Empowered Cooperatives for handholding and credit linkage by NCDC, dovetailed with grant, subsidy, incentives, etc. from the Government of India / State / UT / agencies with the objective of cooperatives actively partaking in Digital India. title: Review of National Cooperation Policy, 2025
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Cooperation Review of National Cooperation Policy, 2025 प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 JUL 2026 5:23PM by PIB Delhi A national-level ‘Policy Implementation and Monitoring Committee’ has been established with a mandate of central-state coordination, troubleshooting implementation bottlenecks, periodic monitoring and evaluation, etc. The ‘Policy Implementation and Monitoring Committee’ held its first meeting on 09.06.2026, the members of the Committee were from Central Ministries/Departments, National Federations/National Cooperative Societies, and representatives and senior officials from State Governments. In its first meeting, it was informed that the NCP was implemented through the Whole-of-Government approach and in the spirit of cooperative federalism. The institutional mechanism for monitoring the implementation of the policy given in   NCP 2025 are as follows: “9.5.1. A ‘National Steering Committee on Cooperation Policy’, chaired by the Union Minister of Cooperation, to be constituted for overall guidance, inter-ministerial coordination, periodic policy review, etc. This committee may include the Hon’ble Minister-in-charge of related Ministries of the Government of India as members, 9.5.2. A national-level ‘Policy Implementation and Monitoring Committee’, chaired by the Union Cooperation Secretary, to be established for central-state coordination, troubleshooting implementation bottlenecks, periodic monitoring and evaluation, etc. It may comprise members, including the Secretary of related Ministries of the Government of India, Secretaries/Principal Secretaries/Additional Chief Secretaries of the Cooperative Department of all States/Union Territories, a representative from NITI Aayog, and Chairpersons/MDs of national cooperative federations/unions/societies, NABARD, NDDB, NCDC, NFDB, NCCT, VAMNICOM, etc.” Both the above committees have been constituted. The policy provides a roadmap for the systematic and holistic development of the cooperative sector. It has 6 strategic pillars, 16 objectives, and 83 recommendations. The Policy enunciates a vision, a mission, and 16 specific objectives to be achieved over the next 10 years. A comprehensive National Cooperative Database (NCD) has been developed by the Ministry of Cooperation with the support of States / UTs. This database provides a single-point access to information on over 8.5 lakh cooperatives societies across 30 economic sectors, having approximately 30 crore members. The data of the Cooperative Societies is collected and updated regularly on the NCD portal by nodal officers appointed by the States/ UTs for this purpose. The State-wise details of cooperative societies across the country are attached as Annexure-A . The NCD plays an important role not only during the formulation of any policy intervention but during policy implementation as well. The database provides critical insights into cooperatives’ geographical coverage, financial performance, etc., and thereby helps implement the policy recommendations. The database serves as an important tool for formation of new PACS, dairy and fisheries primary cooperatives in uncovered and under-covered areas, enables development of a ranking framework, and assists in estimating the economic contribution of cooperative sector in the Indian economy. ***** Annexure-A State-wise details of cooperative societies. title: Cooperative societies in Maharashtra
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Cooperation Cooperative societies in Maharashtra प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 JUL 2026 5:18PM by PIB Delhi As per the National Cooperative Database (NCD), as on 15.07.2026, there are a total of 2,27,177 cooperative societies in Maharashtra. The sector-wise details of total number of cooperative societies, district federations and state federations in Maharashtra, are attached as Annexure-1 . The Government launched the Central Sector project for Computerization of PACS, in 2022. Initially, 63,000 PACS were approved under the project with a total financial outlay of ₹2,516 crore. The project has now been expanded to cover 79,630 PACS with a revised financial outlay of ₹2,925.39 crore. It aims to bring all functional PACS onto a common ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning) based national software. The project also links PACS with NABARD through State Cooperative Banks (StCBs) and District Central Cooperative Banks (DCCBs). A total of 12,178 PACS have been sanctioned under the PACS computerization project in Maharashtra. Under the project, financial assistance of ₹29.14 crore has been provided to Maharashtra. This includes ₹9.14 crore during in FY 2025–26, and ₹20.00 crore in FY 2026–27. Additionally, as on 30.06.2026, NCDC has cumulatively disbursed ₹34,161.54 crore for the development of cooperative sector in Maharashtra. The year-wise details of the amount disbursed during the last five years are given at Annexure-1. The Ministry of Cooperation, since its inception on 06.07.2021, has undertaken several initiatives to realize the vision of “Sahakar-se-Samriddhi” and to strengthen dairy, sugar and agri-cooperatives across the country including Maharashtra. These initiatives include: I. Model Bye-laws for PACS : Enabled PACS to undertake more than 25 business activities, improve governance, transparency and accountability in their operations. Now, PACS can operate as PM-Kisan Samridhi Kendras (PMKSKs), Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Kendras (PMBJKs), Common Service Centres (CSC) etc. II. Cooperative-led White Revolution 2.0: Aims to increase milk procurement by dairy cooperatives by 50% over five years. It also focuses on expanding cooperative coverage, generating employment and promoting women’s empowerment. III. Income Tax Relief: Clarified that cooperative sugar mills are not liable to additional income tax on higher sugarcane prices paid up to Fair and Remunerative or State Advised Price, with effect from April 2016. IV. Tax Relief in Union Budget 2023–24: Allowed sugar cooperatives to claim payments made to sugarcane farmers before AY 2016–17 as expenditure, providing relief of over ₹46,000 crore. V. Financial Support through NCDC: Launched a scheme for ethanol plants, cogeneration plants and working capital. The Ministry released ₹1,000 crore to NCDC, which has disbursed ₹10,005 crore to 56 cooperative sugar mills. VI. Ethanol Blending Programme: Brought cooperative sugar mills at par with private companies for ethanol procurement under the EBP. VII. Reduction in GST on Molasses: Reduced GST on molasses from 28% to 5%, increasing margins and profits for cooperative sugar mills. VIII. Revival of Closed Sugar Mills: Indian Potash Limited has taken an initiative to revive closed cooperative sugar mills on the suggestion of the Ministry of Cooperation. ****** Annexure-1 Sector-wise total number of Primary Societies, District Federations and State Federations in Maharashtra S. title: DRDO inks two major contracts with Industry partners as part of AEW&C MK-II programme
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Defence DRDO inks two major contracts with Industry partners as part of AEW&C MK-II programme प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 JUL 2026 8:19PM by PIB Delhi In a significant boost to Aatmanirbhar Bharat, Centre for Air Borne Systems (CABS), DRDO has signed a contract with AI Engineering Services Limited (AIESL), New Delhi for the conversion of six A321 Aircraft from commercial to green configuration, further leading to the development and production of Airborne Early Warning & Control (AEW&C) MKII Programme. A separate contract was inked with Adani Defence Systems and Technologies (ADSTL), Ahmedabad to engage with the company as Development Cum Production Partner (DcPP) for Mission Systems designed for the AEW&C MKII Programme. The contracts were signed by Director CABS with CEO, AIESL and Head-Airborne Platform, ADSTL in the presence of Defence Secretary and Secretary, Department of Defence R&D and Chairman, DRDO Shri Rajesh Kumar Singh in New Delhi on July 22, 2026. CABS, DRDO with support from ADSTL as DcPP is responsible for integration of mission systems on modified AEW&C MK II Platform, delivered by Airbus Defence & Space (Original Equipment Manufacturer). CABS and ADSTL will also carry out flight testing of the AEW&C MK II aircraft along with the Indian Air Force to obtain certification from airworthiness agencies - Centre for Military Airworthiness and Certification and Directorate General of Aeronautical Quality Assurance. AEW&C Mk II System from DRDO with CABS as the nodal laboratory will provide enhanced endurance, advanced airborne surveillance, secure communication, improved situational awareness and enhanced command and control capabilities. This, in turn, will give a significant boost to the air defence capabilities and aid in neutralising threats across extended ranges. The engagement of industries reaffirms the commitment of the Government to achieve self-reliance for fostering a robust ecosystem towards innovation, research and manufacturing within the country. *** VK/ Savvy (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2288009) आगंतुक पटल  : 57 Ministry of Defence DRDO inks two major contracts with Industry partners as part of AEW&C MK-II programme प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: INDIAN NAVY COMMISSIONS INS MALVAN, THE SECOND OF THE MAHE-CLASS ANTI-SUBMARINE WARFARE SHALLOW WATER CRAFT
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Defence INDIAN NAVY COMMISSIONS INS MALVAN, THE SECOND OF THE MAHE-CLASS ANTI-SUBMARINE WARFARE SHALLOW WATER CRAFT Posted On:
                22 JUL 2026 5:21PM by PIB Delhi INS Malvan, the second of the indigenously designed and built Mahe-class Anti-Submarine Warfare Shallow Water Craft (ASW-SWC), was commissioned at Karwar on 22 Jul 2026. The event was presided over by Air Chief Marshal AP Singh, Chief of the Air Staff, in the presence of Vice Admiral Sanjay Vatsayan, Flag Officer Commanding-in-Chief, Western Naval Command. Other senior naval officers, representatives from Cochin Shipyard Limited (CSL), Kochi, veterans, and distinguished guests were also in attendance. The ship carries deep historical and cultural significance as it derives its name from the historical coastal town of Malvan in Maharashtra, a region intrinsically linked to the illustrious maritime heritage of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj. The vessel also encapsulates the legacy of her predecessor, an inshore Indian Naval Minesweeper that remained in service till 2003. With over 80 percent indigenous content, the ship reinforces the Government of India’s vision of Aatmanirbhar Bharat and India’s expanding ecosystem of naval design, equipment, system integration, and growing self-reliance in defence shipbuilding. The vessel will further bolster coastal defence, littoral security, and enhance Maritime Domain Awareness. The crest of INS Malvan carries the ‘ Bagh Nakha’ (Tiger's Claw), symbolising bravery, warfare tactics, agility, and audacity, resonating with the ship's ethos to attack rapidly and strike silently. The waves surrounding ‘Bagh Nakha’ reflect the vast sea surrounding the coasts and the Indian Navy's unwavering resolve to remain ever vigilant, ever ready, and steadfast in safeguarding the nation's seas and sovereignty. The ship's motto, ‘Silent Claws’ , embodies lethality, stealth, and the ability to strike the adversary swiftly. title: Centre and States are equal partners in building a future-ready education system for Viksit Bharat 2047 – Shri Dharmendra Pradhan
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Education Centre and States are equal partners in building a future-ready education system for Viksit Bharat 2047 – Shri Dharmendra Pradhan Our collective success will be measured by the learning outcomes we achieve and the opportunities we create for every child – Union Minister for Education Shri Dharmendra Pradhan, chairs the two-day Conclave of State and UT Education Ministers to review Centrally Sponsored Schemes of the Department of School Education and Literacy Posted On:
                22 JUL 2026 8:02PM by PIB Delhi Union Minister for Education, Shri Dharmendra Pradhan today said that the Centre and the States are equal partners in strengthening school education. He was chairing the two-day Conclave of State and UT Education Ministers to review Centrally Sponsored Schemes of the Department of School Education and Literacy (DoSEL), Ministry of Education, at the ICAR National Agricultural Science Complex (NASC), New Delhi. In his address, Shri Pradhan emphasised that the Conclave provides a valuab le platform for the Centre and the States and UTs to strengthen cooperation, share best practices, and accelerate the effective implementation of Centrally Sponsored Schemes in line with the vision of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020. He said the deliberations would further reinforce the collective commitment towards building a future-ready, inclusive and high-quality school education system and contribute to the upcoming PRAGATI review chaired by the Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi. Shri Pradhan highlighted the progress made in school education through initiatives such as Samagra Shiksha, PM SHRI, NIPUN Bharat, PM POSHAN and ULLAS, and called upon the States and UTs to continue working together to strengthen foundational literacy and numeracy, empower teachers, leverage technology and AI, promote innovation, and ensure the holistic development of every learner towards the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047 . The Minister urged the states to promote the mother tongue of the child and multilingualism to strengthen foundational learning and improve learning outcomes. Addressing the Conclave, Minister of State for Education and Skill Development and Entrepreneurship Shri Jayant Chaudhary, emphasised on the importance of collaborative efforts between the Centre and States and UTs to strengthen school education and improve educational outcomes. The Conclave aims to advance the shared vision of an equitable, inclusive and quality school education system, contributing to the realisation of the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047. The sessions focussed on strengthening the implementation of Centrally Sponsored Schemes and improving educational outcomes. Education Ministers of States and UTs reaffirmed the importance of Centre–State collaboration, knowledge sharing and the shared commitment to ensuring equitable, inclusive and quality education for every learner. The first day featured presentations by Additional Secretary, DoSEL, Shri Dheeraj Sahu, on Samagra Shiksha and issues for consideration under the PRAGATI framework, and Deputy Director General, DoSEL, Dr. Pankaj K. P. Shreyaskar, on the status of educational indicators in States and UTs. Joint Secretary, DoSEL, Dr. Amarpreet Duggal, and  Economic Advisor, DoSEL ,Ms. A. Srija also participated in the proceedings along with senior officials from the Union Ministry of Education and the States. title: India hosts BRICS Network University Conference and the International Governing Board Meeting, strengthening BRICS Higher Education Cooperation
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Education India hosts BRICS Network University Conference and the International Governing Board Meeting, strengthening BRICS Higher Education Cooperation Traditional and Indigenous Knowledge Systems proposed as a new thematic area under the BRICS Network University International governing board adopts declaration and advances academic cooperation Posted On:
                22 JUL 2026 7:22PM by PIB Delhi As part of India's BRICS Presidency 2026, the Union Ministry of Education successfully convened the International Governing Board (IGB) meeting of the BRICS Network University (BRICS NU) on Tuesday (July 21, 2026) in virtual mode, following the BRICS Network University Conference on Traditional and Indigenous Knowledge Systems held on Monday (July 20, 2026). The two-day engagement brought together government representatives, university leaders, academics and experts from BRICS member countries to strengthen collaboration in higher education, research and innovation. The IGB meeting was inaugurated by the Joint Secretary, Ministry of Education, Dr. K. M. Praphullachandra Sharma, while Dean (International Relations), IIT Bombay, Prof. Sudarshan Kumar, presented an overview of the BRICS Network University, its expanding institutional network and ongoing collaborative initiatives. Member countries also shared updates on their participating universities and academic cooperation activities undertaken during the past year. Representatives from the BRICS member countries, including Brazil, China, Egypt, Indonesia, Iran, Russia, South Africa and the United Arab Emirates, along with university leaders, academics and experts, delivered country interventions showcasing national initiatives and best practices. The deliberations reaffirmed the collective commitment to strengthening the BRICS Network University through enhanced academic cooperation, collaborative research, institutional partnerships and knowledge exchange. A key highlight of the meeting was the presentation of the outcomes of the BRICS Network University Conference on Traditional and Indigenous Knowledge Systems, the first conference of its kind under the BRICS NU framework. The conference deliberated on the mapping, documentation, preservation and responsible digital dissemination of traditional and indigenous knowledge systems, while emphasizing ethical governance, community ownership, equitable benefit-sharing and the responsible use of emerging technologies, including Artificial Intelligence. The Conference also developed Guiding Principles on Strengthening Academic Collaboration on Traditional and Indigenous Knowledge Systems for consideration by the International Governing Board. Recognising the significance of this emerging area of cooperation, the International Governing Board deliberated on the proposal to include Traditional and Indigenous Knowledge Systems as a new International Thematic Group (ITG) under the BRICS Network University. The proposal received broad support from member countries and marks an important milestone towards institutionalising collaboration on traditional knowledge within the BRICS higher education framework. Member countries agreed to continue consultations on the concept note with a view to advancing the proposal. The Governing Board also reviewed the BRICS Network University Action Plan (2025–2028), discussed the development of the new BRICS NU website, considered measures to enhance institutional cooperation, academic mobility and collaborative research, and adopted the BRICS Network University International Governing Board Declaration after detailed deliberations. The meeting reaffirmed the collective commitment of BRICS member countries to strengthening the BRICS Network University as a leading platform for higher education, research, innovation and people-to-people exchanges. India thanked all participating delegations for their constructive engagement and reiterated its commitment to advancing academic cooperation under the theme of its BRICS Presidency, "Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability." ***** RRTN (Release ID: 2287943) Visitor Counter : 106 Read this release in: हिन्दी Ministry of Education India hosts BRICS Network University Conference and the International Governing Board Meeting, strengthening BRICS Higher Education Cooperation Traditional and Indigenous Knowledge Systems proposed as a new thematic area under the BRICS Network University International governing board adopts declaration and advances academic cooperation Posted On:

ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
title: NBA releases Rs 6.67 crore under Access and Benefit Sharing Mechanism for Biodiversity Conservation and Livelihood Support in 11 cotton-growing States
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change NBA releases Rs 6.67 crore under Access and Benefit Sharing Mechanism for Biodiversity Conservation and Livelihood Support in 11 cotton-growing States प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 JUL 2026 8:03PM by PIB Delhi The National Biodiversity Authority (NBA) has released Rs 6.67 crore under the Access and Benefit Sharing (ABS) mechanism to support biodiversity conservation, sustainable utilisation of biological resources and livelihood enhancement in 11 cotton-growing States. The disbursement demonstrates how benefits derived from the commercial utilisation of biological resources are being reinvested in biodiversity conservation and community welfare under the Biological Diversity Act. The benefit-sharing amount of Rs 7.62 crore has been realised from M/s Bayer Science & Innovation Pvt. Ltd. (formerly Monsanto Holdings Pvt. Ltd.) for research involving 25,431 cotton (Gossypium hirsutum) varieties. Cotton occupies a unique place in India's agricultural and economic landscape, with the country serving as a global reservoir of cotton genetic diversity that supports nearly 4-5 crore people across the value chain. Since the biological resources were accessed through traders and intermediaries, identifying individual conservers or benefit claimers was not feasible. To address such situations, the NBA, with the support of an Expert Committee, has developed transparent modalities for the utilisation of ABS amounts. Where the geographical occurrence of a biological resource can be reliably established using published records, the corresponding ABS amount is allocated to the concerned State Biodiversity Boards (SBBs) for biodiversity conservation, sustainable utilisation and socio-economic development of the concerned areas. Where the source cannot be established, the funds are retained in the National Biodiversity Fund and utilised in accordance with Section 27 of the Biological Diversity Act for conservation and sustainable use of biological resources across the country. Applying these modalities, the NBA has allocated Rs 6.67 among eleven cotton-growing States: Maharashtra (Rs 2.41 crore), Gujarat (Rs 1.38 crore), Telangana (Rs 1.06 crore), Karnataka (Rs 0.40 crore), Rajasthan (Rs 0.36 crore), Madhya Pradesh (Rs 0.31 crore), Andhra Pradesh (Rs 0.23 crore), Haryana (Rs 0.23 crore), Odisha (Rs 0.14 crore), Punjab (Rs 0.09 crore) and Tamil Nadu (Rs 0.06 crore). The remaining amount (Rs 0.95 crore) has been earmarked for the NBA as per the Biological Diversity Rules. The allocation is based on the geographical distribution of cotton cultivation using data from the All India Coordinated Research Project on Cotton (AICRP), ICAR, and is proportional to each State's area under cotton cultivation, ensuring a transparent, scientific and equitable distribution of ABS benefits. The allocation will support on-farm and ex-situ conservation of biological resources, documentation and updation of People's Biodiversity Registers, ecosystem restoration, strengthening of Biodiversity Heritage Sites, documentation of traditional knowledge, biodiversity research, development of digital biodiversity databases, capacity building of Biodiversity Management Committees, awareness programmes and livelihood enhancement. These investments will help conserve valuable genetic traits for future crop improvement while empowering local communities as custodians of India's agrobiodiversity. The initiative also establishes a transparent and science-based model for distributing ABS benefits where biological resources are sourced through complex supply chains. By linking benefit-sharing to the verified geographical occurrence of biological resources, it ensures that ABS reaches biodiversity-rich regions even when individual beneficiaries cannot be identified. With this disbursement, the total ABS funds released by the NBA have reached Rs 152.24 crore. The initiative demonstrates how the ABS mechanism transforms the commercial utilisation of biological resources to combine economy, ecology and equity. It also contributes to the implementation of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework, particularly Target 13 on the fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising from the utilisation of genetic resources, while supporting Target 4 on conserving genetic diversity. The National Biodiversity Authority is a statutory body established under the Biological Diversity Act, 2002, functioning under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change. It regulates access to India's biological resources and associated knowledge and implements the Nagoya Protocol's principle of fair and equitable sharing of benefits. ***** VM/GS (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2287985) आगंतुक पटल  : 47 Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change NBA releases Rs 6.67 crore under Access and Benefit Sharing Mechanism for Biodiversity Conservation and Livelihood Support in 11 cotton-growing States प्रविष्टि तिथि:
