ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
title: Senior Officials' Meeting Held in Chandigarh as Part of Ongoing BRICS Health Ministerial Meetings Under India's Chairship
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Senior Officials' Meeting Held in Chandigarh as Part of Ongoing BRICS Health Ministerial Meetings Under India's Chairship Expanded BRICS Represents an Unprecedented Opportunity to Shape the Future of Global Health Through Innovation and Consensus-Driven Solutions: Union Health Secretary India Identifies Nine Priority Areas Under BRICS Health Track to Build Resilient and Inclusive Health Systems Union Health Secretary Inaugurates FSSAI, NHA and Ministry of AYUSH Exhibition Pavilions at BRICS Health Ministerial Summit प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 JUL 2026 6:42PM by PIB Delhi As part of the ongoing BRICS Health Ministerial Meeting being held under India's BRICS Chairship, the Senior Officials' Meeting was held today in Chandigarh. The meeting was inaugurated by Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava, Union Health Secretary, Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India, who welcomed the delegates and underscored the importance of strengthening collaboration among BRICS nations to address evolving global public health challenges through cooperation, innovation and equitable access to healthcare. In her inaugural address, Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava, Union Health Secretary, welcomed the delegates to Chandigarh and stated that the city's ethos of innovation, sustainability and thoughtful development aptly reflects India's BRICS Chairship theme, "Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability." She noted that the theme assumes greater significance in the evolving global health landscape, where increasingly complex and interconnected health challenges call for stronger collaboration, cooperation and collective action among nations. Highlighting the importance of the expanded BRICS grouping, the Union Health Secretary said that the bloc, representing a significant share of the world's population, scientific expertise and manufacturing capacity, provides an unprecedented opportunity to shape the future of global health through innovation and consensus-driven solutions. She emphasized that, guided by the spirit of partnership and shared responsibility, India has identified nine priority areas under the BRICS Health Track to strengthen resilient, equitable and inclusive health systems. She informed that these priority areas focus on strengthening health infrastructure; enhancing preparedness for future health emergencies through robust surveillance systems and laboratory networks; leveraging digital health technologies; integrating traditional medicine into healthcare systems; strengthening regulatory frameworks; developing a skilled health workforce; promoting collaborative research and development; and ensuring timely, affordable and equitable access to healthcare services, essential medicines and medical products. The Union Health Secretary further highlighted India's flagship initiatives under the BRICS Health Track—the BRICS Mission for Healthy Lifestyle and the proposed BRICS Network of Centres of Excellence for Mental Health—which reinforce the collective commitment of BRICS countries towards preventive and promotive healthcare, specialized care, knowledge sharing and deeper cooperation in addressing emerging public health challenges. Referring to the draft BRICS Health Ministers' Declaration, Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava said that the document reflects the collective vision and outcome of extensive technical consultations among the Member States. She expressed confidence that the deliberations during the Senior Officials' Meeting would help build consensus on the remaining provisions of the Declaration, paving the way for its adoption at the 16th BRICS Health Ministers' Meeting. She also emphasized the importance of strengthening cooperation in areas such as Nuclear Medicine and supporting the activities of the BRICS Vaccine Research and Development Centre, reaffirming the shared commitment of BRICS nations towards collaborative research, innovation and global health security. The Union Health Secretary also inaugurated the exhibition pavilions of the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI), the National Health Authority (NHA) and the Ministry of AYUSH. The pavilions showcased India's flagship initiatives and innovations in food safety, digital health, traditional systems of medicine and integrated healthcare delivery, offering delegates an opportunity to experience the country's transformative health initiatives. The deliberations during the Senior Officials' Meeting focused on finalizing the BRICS Health Ministerial Declaration. Senior officials held detailed discussions on the key priority areas under the BRICS Health Track, reaffirming their shared commitment to strengthening cooperation in addressing common public health challenges. The discussions covered priority areas including strengthening primary healthcare, advancing Universal Health Coverage, promoting digital health and health innovation, enhancing preparedness and response to public health emergencies, addressing antimicrobial resistance, strengthening pharmaceutical cooperation, improving access to quality and affordable medical products, and fostering collaboration in traditional medicine and health research. The participating countries reiterated the importance of collaborative research, knowledge sharing, capacity building and technology exchange in advancing resilient and equitable health systems. The meeting also emphasized the need for stronger multilateral cooperation to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals related to health. ***** SR HFW/BRICS Senior Official’s Meeting/22 July 2026/1 (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2287898) आगंतुक पटल  : 95 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: हिन्दी Ministry of Health and Family Welfare Senior Officials' Meeting Held in Chandigarh as Part of Ongoing BRICS Health Ministerial Meetings Under India's Chairship Expanded BRICS Represents an Unprecedented Opportunity to Shape the Future of Global Health Through Innovation and Consensus-Driven Solutions: Union Health Secretary India Identifies Nine Priority Areas Under BRICS Health Track to Build Resilient and Inclusive Health Systems Union Health Secretary Inaugurates FSSAI, NHA and Ministry of AYUSH Exhibition Pavilions at BRICS Health Ministerial Summit प्रविष्टि तिथि:

The meeting was inaugurated by Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava, Union Health Secretary, Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India, who welcomed the delegates and underscored the importance of strengthening collaboration among BRICS nations to address evolving global public health challenges through cooperation, innovation and equitable access to healthcare. In her inaugural address, Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava, Union Health Secretary, welcomed the delegates to Chandigarh and stated that the city's ethos of innovation, sustainability and thoughtful development aptly reflects India's BRICS Chairship theme, "Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability." She noted that the theme assumes greater significance in the evolving global health landscape, where increasingly complex and interconnected health challenges call for stronger collaboration, cooperation and collective action among nations. Highlighting the importance of the expanded BRICS grouping, the Union Health Secretary said that the bloc, representing a significant share of the world's population, scientific expertise and manufacturing capacity, provides an unprecedented opportunity to shape the future of global health through innovation and consensus-driven solutions. title: ICMR-NIN-led ‘Let’s Fix Our Food’ Consortium Releases Policy Priorities to Promote Healthier Diets for Children and Adolescents
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Health and Family Welfare ICMR-NIN-led ‘Let’s Fix Our Food’ Consortium Releases Policy Priorities to Promote Healthier Diets for Children and Adolescents Policy document outlines evidence-based recommendations to create healthier food environments and improve dietary behaviours among children and adolescents NITI Aayog Member (Health) Dr. M. Srinivas launches policy document during LFOF Dissemination and Consultation Workshop in New Delhi Posted On:
                22 JUL 2026 6:03PM by PIB Delhi The Indian Council of Medical Research–National Institute of Nutrition (ICMR-NIN)-led 'Let's Fix Our Food' (LFOF) Consortium today released a policy document titled 'Priority Policy Actions to Promote Healthier Diets and Food Environments for Children and Adolescents in India', outlining evidence-based recommendations to support healthier food environments and improve dietary behaviours among children and adolescents across the country. The policy document was launched by Dr. M. Srinivas, Member (Health), NITI Aayog, during the LFOF Dissemination and Consultation Workshop held at the India Habitat Centre, New Delhi, in the presence of Dr. Bharati Kulkarni, Director, ICMR-NIN, Prof. (Dr.) K. Srinath Reddy, Founder President, Public Health Foundation of India (PHFI), and senior representatives from the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, FSSAI, UNICEF India, Resolve to Save Lives (RTSL), consortium partner institutions, researchers, development partners and youth representatives. The Let's Fix Our Food (LFOF) Consortium is a multi-institutional national platform led by ICMR-NIN, with participation from Resolve to Save Lives (RTSL) India, UNICEF India, Global Health Advocacy Incubator (GHAI), PHFI, WHO, FSSAI, IEG, WFP, Lady Irwin College, IFPRI, Deakin University and other national and international partners. Through research, policy analysis, advocacy and stakeholder engagement, the Consortium seeks to support India's efforts to prevent diet-related non-communicable diseases by transforming food environments, particularly for children and adolescents. The publication brings together nearly three years of multidisciplinary research, stakeholder consultations and policy dialogues. It sets out policy recommendations across key areas, including healthy school food environments, nutrition literacy, front-of-pack nutrition labelling, regulation of marketing of unhealthy food to children, taxation of foods high in fat, salt and sugar (HFSS), healthier dietary fats, salt reduction, low-sodium salt substitutes, social and behaviour change communication, youth engagement and fiscal measures to promote healthier diets. Speaking on the occasion, Dr. M. Srinivas, Member (Health), NITI Aayog, said, "Evidence-based, multisectoral policy action is essential to create healthier food environments for children and adolescents. Collaborative initiatives such as the Let's Fix Our Food Consortium are important for addressing the growing burden of overweight, obesity and diet-related non-communicable diseases in India." Dr. Bharati Kulkarni, Director, ICMR-NIN, said, "ICMR-NIN is committed to generating high-quality evidence and fostering partnerships that translate research into public health action. The policy recommendations reflect the collective efforts of researchers, policymakers, development partners and young people working towards healthier food environments for India's future generations." Prof. (Dr.) K. Srinath Reddy, Founder President, Public Health Foundation of India (PHFI), underscored the need for comprehensive policy interventions addressing the commercial, social and environmental determinants of unhealthy diets, and called for sustained action to protect children and adolescents from obesogenic food environments. The workshop also witnessed the launch of several knowledge products developed under the Consortium, including the LFOF website, the Nutrition Environment Assessment Toolkit for Schools (NEAT-S) and its report, an e-learning module on understanding food labels, and a suite of ICMR-NIN educational resources on fats, sugars and salt to strengthen nutrition literacy among children and adolescents. Marie-Claude Desilets, Chief of Nutrition, UNICEF India, said, "Malnutrition is no longer only about undernutrition. Rising obesity, driven by unhealthy diets, challenges healthy growth among children and adolescents. The release of these ten policy briefs and the Nutrition Environment Assessment Toolkit for Schools (NEAT-S) marks a step towards creating policies for healthier school food environments. Every child has the right to grow up in a food environment that enables them to thrive, learn and achieve their full potential." Dr. Syed Imran Farooq, Executive Director, Resolve to Save Lives (RTSL), highlighted the need to reduce excess salt, fat and sugar intake alongside food policies that support healthier food environments and lower the burden of cardiovascular diseases and other health threats. He also acknowledged the leadership of ICMR-NIN and reaffirmed RTSL's commitment to the shared vision of healthier food environments across India. The consultation showcased new evidence generated by consortium partners on school food environments, unhealthy food marketing, nutrition education, dietary behaviours, fiscal policy options and nutrition environment assessments across multiple states. The workshop concluded with thematic discussions on translating evidence into actionable policy recommendations to support healthier food environments for children and adolescents. Background The Let's Fix Our Food Consortium was established to generate evidence and catalyse policy action for healthier food environments in India, with a special focus on children and adolescents. The policy priorities released today draw on multidisciplinary research and consultations and seek to support efforts to prevent diet-related non-communicable diseases through coordinated, evidence-informed action. title: BHANDEWADI’S URBAN FACELIFT
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs BHANDEWADI’S URBAN FACELIFT TURNING LEGACY WASTE INTO OPPORTUNITY प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 JUL 2026 5:59PM by PIB Delhi Under the Swachh Bharat Mission–Urban 2.0, with a focused thrust on achieving the Lakshya Zero Dumpsite, scientific remediation of legacy waste is being undertaken across States and Urban Local Bodies in a structured and time-bound manner. Cities are increasingly adopting bio-mining and advanced processing technologies, while continuous monitoring and systematic clearance of legacy dumpsites are strengthening the transition towards environmentally sustainable urban ecosystems. Nagpur stands out as a leading example of scientifically transforming a legacy dumpsite into a sustainable waste management system. Nagpur, a major urban and economic centre in Central India, has emerged as one of the rapidly expanding cities in the region. With accelerated urbanisation and a population exceeding 30 lakh, the city has witnessed a consistent increase in municipal solid waste generation from households, markets, institutions, commercial establishments, and public spaces. Over time, a significant proportion of this waste was directed to the Bhandewadi dumping yard, which gradually developed into a major legacy waste site, thereby posing considerable environmental and operational challenges for the city administration. Recognising the urgent need to shift from open dumping to scientific waste management, the Nagpur Municipal Corporation (NMC) undertook a landmark initiative to scientifically remediate the Bhandewadi dumpsite and convert it into a sustainable waste processing ecosystem aligned with principles of circular economy and environmental protection. The increasing dependence on landfill disposal further intensified the need for a structured and long-term scientific intervention to ensure environmentally safe waste management practices for the city. Through systematic excavation, segregation and processing of legacy waste, more than 10 lakh metric tons of accumulated waste was successfully treated. This intervention not only eliminated a major environmental burden but also enabled the reclamation of acres of valuable land, previously locked under waste deposits. Following remediation, the site was transformed into a modern integrated Municipal Solid Waste Processing Facility. The facility now operates with multiple scientific systems including Material Recovery Facilities (MRFs), composting units, RDF generation systems, leachate treatment infrastructure, and advanced environmental monitoring mechanisms. This integrated approach ensures that waste is no longer viewed as a liability but as a resource that can be scientifically processed and recovered. To strengthen operational efficiency and environmental compliance, Nagpur introduced a range of technological innovations at the facility. Advanced systems such as trommels, ballistic separators, composting units, SCADA monitoring, CCTV surveillance and dust control measures have improved waste processing, enabled real-time monitoring and ensured environmental safety. The transformation of Bhandewadi has also delivered significant environmental benefits for the city. There has been a marked reduction in landfill dependency, improved air, water and soil quality, and enhanced public health conditions in surrounding areas. The shift towards scientific recycling and resource recovery has further strengthened Nagpur’s transition towards a sustainable urban environment. In parallel, the city has expanded its waste management infrastructure through additional projects such as composting plants, modular waste processing units, Material Recovery Facilities and Construction & Demolition (C&D) waste processing systems. These initiatives collectively enhance the city’s capacity for decentralised and efficient waste management. The key achievements of this transformation are significant. Over 10 lakh metric tons of legacy waste has been processed, approximately 55 acres of land has been reclaimed, and a robust integrated waste processing infrastructure has been established. The initiative has also strengthened circular economy practices through scientific segregation, recycling and sustainable resource recovery. The remediation of the Bhandewadi dumpsite serves as a compelling example of how scientific planning, technological innovation, and sustained implementation can fundamentally transform urban waste management systems. It illustrates the shift from legacy waste burdens towards structured, sustainable, and future-ready infrastructure. **** SK (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2287849) आगंतुक पटल  : 97 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: हिन्दी Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs BHANDEWADI’S URBAN FACELIFT TURNING LEGACY WASTE INTO OPPORTUNITY प्रविष्टि तिथि:

The transformation of Bhandewadi has also delivered significant environmental benefits for the city. There has been a marked reduction in landfill dependency, improved air, water and soil quality, and enhanced public health conditions in surrounding areas. The shift towards scientific recycling and resource recovery has further strengthened Nagpur’s transition towards a sustainable urban environment. In parallel, the city has expanded its waste management infrastructure through additional projects such as composting plants, modular waste processing units, Material Recovery Facilities and Construction & Demolition (C&D) waste processing systems. These initiatives collectively enhance the city’s capacity for decentralised and efficient waste management. The key achievements of this transformation are significant. Over 10 lakh metric tons of legacy waste has been processed, approximately 55 acres of land has been reclaimed, and a robust integrated waste processing infrastructure has been established. The initiative has also strengthened circular economy practices through scientific segregation, recycling and sustainable resource recovery. The remediation of the Bhandewadi dumpsite serves as a compelling example of how scientific planning, technological innovation, and sustained implementation can fundamentally transform urban waste management systems. It illustrates the shift from legacy waste burdens towards structured, sustainable, and future-ready infrastructure. **** SK (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2287849)

title: Comprehensive Infrastructure and Welfare Initiatives Strengthen Haj Management for Indian Pilgrims
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Minority Affairs Comprehensive Infrastructure and Welfare Initiatives Strengthen Haj Management for Indian Pilgrims प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 JUL 2026 5:16PM by PIB Delhi The Government, through the Ministry of Minority Affairs and the Haj Committee of India, in coordination with the concerned authorities in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, has undertaken various initiatives to modernise and enhance the infrastructure and facilities for Indian Haj pilgrims. Some of the major initiatives are as follows: Improved Infrastructure at Mina Camps: The traditional accommodation arrangements at Mina have been upgraded by providing sofa-cum-beds, ensuring greater comfort, better utilisation of available space and improved living conditions for pilgrims during their stay. High-Speed Train Connectivity: Indian Haj pilgrims are facilitated to travel between Makkah and Madinah through the High-Speed Rail, which has significantly reduced travel time, improved safety, and enhanced overall travel convenience. Haj Suvidha App: The Ministry has developed the Haj Suvidha App, a comprehensive digital platform that enables pilgrims to access important Haj-related services such as travel details, accommodation information, baggage tracking, emergency contacts, grievance redressal, health-related information, and other essential services, thereby improving communication and service delivery throughout the pilgrimage. Hotel-Style Accommodation in Makkah: Hotel-style accommodation has been arranged for Indian Haj pilgrims in Makkah with improved amenities and services, ensuring enhanced comfort, better accessibility, and a more convenient stay during the Haj period. The Government has undertaken several measures to improve coordination between the Ministry, the Haj Committee of India, and State Haj Committees for the preparations for Haj-2026. These include strengthened institutional coordination through periodic review meetings, issuance of detailed guidelines and timelines for all operational activities, and regular consultations to streamline accommodation, transport, training, and other logistical arrangements. The allocation of Haj quota among States and Union Territories is made in proportion to their Muslim population as per the latest applicable Census data. Accordingly, there is no separate proposal under consideration for increasing the Haj quota of the State of Tamil Nadu. The Government has taken several initiatives to ensure the safety, comfort and logistical convenience of Haj pilgrims, with special emphasis on senior citizens and first-time pilgrims. The major initiatives are as follows: Mandatory Companion for Elderly Pilgrims: Pilgrims aged 65 years and above are required to be accompanied by a companion to ensure adequate assistance and support throughout the pilgrimage. Comprehensive Insurance Coverage: Every Haj pilgrim is provided with insurance coverage of up to ₹6.25 lakh, offering financial protection in the event of unforeseen contingencies during the Haj journey. SHI Ratio: For Haj 2026, the State Haj Inspector ratio has been improved to 1:150, ensuring better accessibility and prompt services for pilgrims. Pre-Departure Training: All selected Haj pilgrims are imparted comprehensive orientation and training before their departure to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, covering pilgrimage rituals, travel procedures, health advisories, safety measures, and the use of digital services. Medical Infrastructure in Saudi Arabia: Medical infrastructure comprising hospitals, medical centres and dispensaries is established at key pilgrimage locations in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia to provide timely and quality healthcare services during the Haj period. The Government deputes qualified doctors, paramedics and other medical personnel to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia to provide medical assistance and emergency healthcare services to Indian Haj pilgrims. These initiatives collectively aim to provide a safer, more comfortable and pilgrim-friendly Haj experience, particularly for senior citizens and first-time Haj travellers. This information was given by Union Minister of Minority Affairs Shri Kiren Rijiju in a written reply in Rajya Sabha today. ***** AK/MR (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2287778) आगंतुक पटल  : 58 Ministry of Minority Affairs Comprehensive Infrastructure and Welfare Initiatives Strengthen Haj Management for Indian Pilgrims प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Government Enhances Digital Governance and Pilgrim Welfare for Haj 2026
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Minority Affairs Government Enhances Digital Governance and Pilgrim Welfare for Haj 2026 प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 JUL 2026 5:15PM by PIB Delhi The Government has undertaken several digital initiatives to improve the management of the Haj pilgrimage for Indian pilgrims during Haj 2026. The major initiatives are as follows: Haj Suvidha App 2.0: The Ministry has launched Haj Suvidha App 2.0, an enhanced digital platform providing pilgrims with end-to-end information and services relating to their Haj journey. The App facilitates access to travel schedules, accommodation details, baggage information, emergency contacts, SOS, health-related information, important advisories, and grievance redressal, thereby improving communication and service delivery. Pilgrims can register and track grievances through the Haj Suvidha App, facilitating timely resolution and improved service delivery. Online Haj Application and Selection: The Haj application process is conducted through an online portal & Haj Suvidha App, and the selection of pilgrims is carried out through a transparent, computerised process, ensuring efficiency and transparency. Online Payment System: Pilgrims can make Haj-related payments through secure online payment modes, facilitating timely and convenient financial transactions. Online Flight Selection: Pilgrims are provided with the facility to indicate their preferred flight dates and timings through the online system, subject to operational feasibility, thereby improving convenience and travel planning. Digital Submission of Passports: The requirement for physical submission of passports has been dispensed with. Pilgrims can submit passport details digitally, reducing paperwork, processing time and the need for repeated visits to State/UT Haj Committees. Digital Accommodation and Pilgrim Information: Details relating to accommodation, flight details and other pilgrim-specific services are made available digitally through the Haj Suvidha App and the online Haj portal, enabling pilgrims to access information conveniently. title: National Commission for Minorities Promotes Dialogue and Inclusive Development through National Outreach Initiatives
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Minority Affairs National Commission for Minorities Promotes Dialogue and Inclusive Development through National Outreach Initiatives प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 JUL 2026 5:14PM by PIB Delhi The details of seminars and conference organised by National Commission for Minorities (NCM) are at Annexure . NCM has conducted a study on the subject “ Contribution of Jain Community in the Field of Education” during 2026. The study documents the historical evolution, institutional contribution and educational philosophy of the Jain community in India. It captures the role of Jain trusts, philanthropists, educational institutions and community organisations in promoting learning, research, scholarships, value-based education and inclusive access to education. National Commission for Minorities (NCM), in discharge of its advisory and facilitative mandate, organized Conference of State Minorities Commissions on the 19 th May 2026 at New Delhi, which was attended by representatives of State Minorities Commissions, including the Maharashtra State Minorities Commission, along with officials of State Governments and Union Territories. The Conference served as a platform to deliberate on institutional strengthening, administrative coordination, grievance redressal mechanisms, and the exchange of best practices for enhancing outreach and improving the delivery of welfare measures for minority communities. The Commission also organized a series of national seminars on the Buddhist, Jain and Parsi communities during 2026 to facilitate dialogue, research and awareness on issues concerning minority communities and to encourage greater dissemination of information on Government welfare initiatives. During these events, the Government's commitment towards the welfare and inclusive development of minority communities was highlighted alongwith various welfare initiatives and programmes. **** Annexure Details of the seminars, conference and outreach progammes organized by National Commission for Minorities during 2026 National Seminar on "Buddhism in Modern India: Navigating Cultural and Social Pathways" (27.02.2026, New Delhi) The National Commission for Minorities (NCM) organized a National seminar on “Buddhism in Modern India: Navigating Cultural and Social Pathways” on 27.02.2026 in New Delhi. The Seminar was graced by Hon’ble Minister of Minority Affairs, and Hon’ble Minister of State for Minority Affairs. The seminar focused on heritage preservation, education, youth engagement and the role of Buddhist philosophy in promoting peace and social harmony. The seminar brought together policymakers, scholars, spiritual leaders, and community representatives to deliberate on the evolving role of Buddhism in India’s socio-cultural landscape. National Seminar on "The Contribution of the Jain Community to the Indian Economy, Education and Philanthropy" (23.04.2026, Indore) National Commission for Minorities (NCM), in collaboration with Devi Ahilya Vishwavidyalaya (DAVV), Indore, organized a National Seminar on “The Contribution of the Jain Community to the Indian Economy, Education, and Philanthropy” on 23.4.20226 in Indore. The Seminar was graced by Hon’ble Minister of State for Minority Affairs. The seminar brought together scholars, academicians, industrialists, philanthropists, students, and members of the Jain community to discuss the community’s significant role in nation-building. The seminar focused on the preservation of Parsi heritage, socio-economic development, demographic challenges and the community's invaluable contribution to nation-building. title: PM VIKAS Scheme Advances Skill Development and Entrepreneurship for Minority Communities
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Minority Affairs PM VIKAS Scheme Advances Skill Development and Entrepreneurship for Minority Communities प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 JUL 2026 5:13PM by PIB Delhi The Ministry reviews the implementation of the PM VIKAS Scheme on a regular basis at various levels to assess progress, address operational challenges and strengthen implementation. Periodic review meetings are conducted with Project Implementing Agencies (PIAs), National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC), Awarding Bodies and other stakeholders. The PM VIKAS scheme guidelines were approved in January 2025, and targets under the scheme were allocated under the three different components of the scheme viz. a) skilling and training, b ) women leadership and entrepreneurship and c) education to be covered through 59 Project implementing agencies. Out of the total allocated, state wise number of enrolled candidates are as follows: States/UTs Enrolled Candidates Andhra Pradesh 2,952 Assam 14,521 Bihar 1,760 Delhi 2,112 Haryana 769 Jammu And Kashmir 7,491 Jharkhand 5,593 Karnataka 1,409 Kerala 607 Madhya Pradesh 4,161 Maharashtra 5,216 Manipur 60 Meghalaya 510 Nagaland 370 Punjab 8,349 Rajasthan 488 Sikkim - Tamil Nadu 381 Telangana 2,422 Tripura 984 Uttar Pradesh 17,634 Uttarakhand 2,845 West Bengal 284 Total 80,918 (c & d): The implementation of the PM VIKAS Scheme and related consultations with stakeholders have highlighted certain areas requiring strengthening. These include strengthening industry linkages and placement opportunities through greater focus on apprenticeships, On-the-Job Training (OJT), verified placements and alignment of training programmes with emerging and future skill requirements. To improve employment outcomes and self-employment opportunities under PM VIKAS, the Government has adopted a multi-pronged approach. The Scheme provides industry-aligned skilling in emerging sectors through reputed institutions and industry-linked Project Implementing Agencies. To strengthen employment linkages, the Ministry also organizes stakeholder consultations to facilitate placement opportunities for trained candidates. The Scheme also envisages career counselling, entrepreneurship development training, mentoring support through Business Mentors/Udyami Mitras and integrates credit linkages with the National Minorities Development & Finance Corporation (NMDFC) to facilitate access to concessional finance for self-employment and enterprise development. This information was given by Union Minister of Minority Affairs Shri Kiren Rijiju in a written reply in Rajya Sabha today. ***** AK/MR (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2287772) आगंतुक पटल  : 76 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी Ministry of Minority Affairs PM VIKAS Scheme Advances Skill Development and Entrepreneurship for Minority Communities प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: India’s Installed Wind Power Capacity Reaches 57,443 MW as on June 30, 2026
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of New and Renewable Energy India’s Installed Wind Power Capacity Reaches 57,443 MW as on June 30, 2026 Posted On:
                22 JUL 2026 4:32PM by PIB Delhi The Government has taken several initiatives for development of Renewable Energy including wind energy in the country. The details are placed as Annexure-I . As on 30.06.2026, the total installed capacity of wind energy projects in the country is 57443 MW. The state wise details of installed capacity of wind energy projects are placed as Annexure-II. Further, the power generation from wind energy projects during FY 2025-26 was 106 billion units. The state wise details of power generation from wind energy projects during FY 2025-26 is placed as Annexure-III. The power generation from wind energy projects has increased during last three financial years. The details of wind power generation and annual wind capacity addition during last three financial years are as follows; S. No. Year Wind Capacity Addition (MW) Wind Power Generation (in billion units) 1 2023-24 3253 83 2 2024-25 4151 83 3 2025-26 6057 106 As per GWEC Report 2026, India ranked 4 th position globally in wind energy installation till 31 st Dec, 2025. Annexure-I Government has taken several initiatives to promote development of Renewable Energy including wind energy in the country. These, inter alia, include; Laying of new transmission lines and creating new sub-station capacity has been funded under the Green Energy Corridor Scheme for evacuation of renewable power. Inter State Transmission System (ISTS) charges have been waived for inter-state sale of solar and wind power for projects commissioned by 30th June 2025 and to be commissioned thereafter with graded ISTS charges. To augment transmission infrastructure needed for steep RE trajectory, transmission plan has been prepared till 2030. Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) has been permitted up to 100 percent under the automatic route. To boost RE consumption, Renewable Purchase Obligation (RPO) followed by Renewable Consumption Obligation (RCO) trajectory has been notified till 2029-30. title: PARLIAMENT QUESTION: NATIONAL STANDARDS FOR CIVIL SERVICE TRAINING INSTITUTIONS
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions PARLIAMENT QUESTION: NATIONAL STANDARDS FOR CIVIL SERVICE TRAINING INSTITUTIONS प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 JUL 2026 4:37PM by PIB Delhi The National Standards for Civil Service Training Institutions (NSCSTI) has been revised and launched as NSCSTI 2.0 on 18.07.2025. The revision of NSCSTI was undertaken to ensure alignment with the evolving objectives of Mission Karmayogi and the strategic role of Civil Service Training Institutions (CSTIs) in institutionalizing continuous learning and delivering competency- based training. A review of the implementation of NSCSTI was undertaken through a structured consultative process, wherein a national level workshop with accredited CSTIs was convened to obtain detailed feedback on the existing framework. The findings from the review formed the basis for restructuring the framework and rationalization of the assessment metrics from 59 to 43 under NSCSTI 2.0. The assessment metrics focus on themes like course design, faculty development, resource and training targets, digitization and training delivery, training evaluation and quality assurance, governance and operation functions of the training institution. Measures taken to strengthen the quality and standardization of civil services training include the preparation of Quality Improvement Plans (QIPs) based on gap analysis, supported by mentoring from higher-rated institutions; faculty development through targeted training programmes; support for the digitisation of training content; strengthening of governance, procurement, and training management processes; and the establishment of a continuous benchmarking and collaborative ecosystem to facilitate resource sharing, real-time data-driven decision-making, and long-term institutional development across Central and State training institutions. Training Institutes are awarded 1-Star to 5-Star ratings as per their performance in the assessment. So far 209 Institutes have been accredited, out of which 25 have received 4-star or above rating. The remaining institutions have ratings 3- star or below. This information was given by Union Minister of State for Prime Minister’s office and Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Atomic Energy and Space, Dr. Jitendra Singh, in a written reply in the Lok Sabha today. ***** NKR/AK/NM (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2287730) आगंतुक पटल  : 131 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions PARLIAMENT QUESTION: NATIONAL STANDARDS FOR CIVIL SERVICE TRAINING INSTITUTIONS प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: RailOne App Gains Widespread Popularity Among Passengers with 4.55 Crore Downloads and Average Daily Ticket Bookings of 9.65 Lakh
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Railways RailOne App Gains Widespread Popularity Among Passengers with 4.55 Crore Downloads and Average Daily Ticket Bookings of 9.65 Lakh Indian Railways Strengthens Anti-Fraud Measures; Over 6.68 Crore User Accounts Deactivated For Unusual Mobile Numbers, Email Domains, IP Addresses Since January 2024 530 Suspicious Booking Complaints Lodged on the National Cyber Crime Portal and 13,343 Suspicious Email Domains Blocked in the year 2025-26 & 2026-27 (till 30.06.2026) 89% of Reserved Tickets Booked Online in Indian Railways Out of 65.08 Crore Tickets Booked During June 2025–June 2026; 11% Booked Through Counters प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 JUL 2026 4:28PM by PIB Delhi To improve overall passenger experience, Railways has launched RailOne App on 01.07.2025. The App can be downloaded from Android Play Store and Apple App Store.  This App enables passengers to book reserved as well as unreserved tickets on mobile phone. This App combines all the public facing services of Indian Railways like reserved ticketing, unreserved ticketing and platform ticketing, train enquiry, PNR enquiry, Railmadad, etc. into a single platform. This, in effect, brings the Passenger reservation system facility to passenger's palm. Till date more than 4.55 crore downloads of this app have been done. On an average, about, 9.65 lakh tickets are being booked on the RailOne App Daily (2.75 lakh reserved and 6.89 lakh Unreserved). The passengers can book both reserved and unreserved tickets very conveniently using this app. RailMadad is Indian Railways grievance redressal mechanism that provides passengers an integrated platform for grievance redressal, seeking assistance and inquiry. In RailMadad, passengers can seek redressal through multiple channels such as Helpline number-139, RailMadad Web, App and SMS. RailMadad features an automated complaint assignment and auto-escalation system to ensure the timely redressal of grievances. Grievances and calls for assistance are captured in more than 30 Train and Station categories to ensure smooth journey. In addition, during the financial year 2025–26, RailMadad provided assistance in 6,94,368 cases with 89.49% excellent and satisfactory feedback. The platform also enables passengers to share feedback on the resolution of their grievances, helping Indian Railways monitor service quality and improve passenger satisfaction. Details of grievances resolved during last three years is as under: - Year % of total grievances resolved 2023-2024 99.98% 2024-2025 99.99% 2025-2026 99.98% The reservation ticket booking system of Indian Railways is a robust and highly secure system equipped with industry-standard, state-of-the-art cyber security controls. Indian Railways has taken the following measures to safeguard the system from cyber attacks and to prevent auto filling of forms by hacking tools for curbing frauds in tatkal ticketing booking through internet: 1. Aadhaar authentication to book tatkal  tickets –  A provision has been made to allow only Aaadhar authenticated passengers to book Tatkal tickets online. It helps in preventing the creation and operation of fake or unauthorized agent-controlled multiple user account by imposing a uniqueness constraint.  This measure acts as an effective safeguard against account multiplication and automated misuse, thereby ensuring fair allocation of tatkal tickets.  It has enhanced transparency in the online tatkal booking system.  To curb misuse and improve fairness in tatkal bookings, Aadhaar based One-Time Password (OTP) verification for online tatkal ticket booking has also been introduced on selected trains. 2. Application layer Security Control -- Several application level security controls have been implemented at multiple levels to avoid scripting, Brute-Force Attack and DDoS (Distributed Denial of Service) attacks.  A number of security measures have also been applied for handling the OWASP (Open Web Application Security Project) for application security vulnerability. 3. Network and Infrastructure Layer Security Controls – The entire ICT (Information and Communication Technology) infrastructure has been deployed on high availability mode to minimize failures. The system is protected by industry-standard state-of-the-art and data centre grade network along with security equipment consisting of network firewalls, network intrusion prevention system, application delivery controllers and web application firewalls. The system is also protected from volume-based DDoS (Distributed Denial of Service) attacks with ISP (Internet Service Provider) layer, DDoS Detection and Mitigation Services through multiple ISPs with aggregated DDoS mitigation capacity of nearly 30 Gbps. The enterprise level Content Delivery Network (CDN), anti-bot, secure DNS and Web Application Firewall (WAF) services for enhanced security, better customer experience, regulating web traffic load, resource optimisation and threat mitigation have been deployed. For comprehensive cyber threat intelligence services, specialized agencies have been engaged to undertake Deep-Dark Web Monitoring, Digital Risk Protection and improve incident response. 4. Physical Security Controls – The system is hosted in a captive data center facility Chanakyapuri, New Delhi secured with CCTV footage and restricted physical access.  The facility is ISO 27001 (Information Security Management System) certified. 5. Security Audit and Monitoring -   The system is integrated with CERT-In TSAP (Threat & Situational Awareness Projects) for round the clock monitoring of security incidents and events. Security log monitoring of the system is being done by on-premises security team for detection and mitigation of security incidents. 6. Administrative measures – Several anti-fraud measures have been adopted to prevent unauthorized access and to ensure seamless booking for genuine users. Rigorous revalidation and verification of user accounts have been done. During the period 01.01.2024 to 30.06.2026, more than 6.68 crore user accounts were deactivated and more than 6.22 crore user accounts were put under temporary suspension with option of revalidation. IRCTC has not deactivated any user account due to non-linking of Aadhaar. IRCTC adopts broad parameters for identifying suspicious user IDs on the basis of unusual mobile numbers, email domains, IP Addresses, etc. Regular security audits of the reservation system are carried out by CERT-In empanelled information Security Audit Agencies.  Moreover, internet traffic related to the ticketing system is continuously monitored by CERT-In and the National Critical Information Infrastructure Protection Centre (NCIIPC) to detect and prevent cyber attacks. 530 complaints have been lodged on the National Cyber Crime Portal pertaining to suspicious bookings in the year 2025-26 & 2026-27 (till 30.06.2026). 13,343 suspicious email domains have been blocked in the year 2025-26 & 2026-27 (till 30.06.2026). Only Aadhaar Verified Users are allowed to book Tatkal tickets and ARP (Advance Reservation Period) tickets. 7. Systemic Measures (Content Delivery Network and Anti BOT) - To optimize system performance, Indian Railway has implemented a Content Delivery Network (CDN) to offload static content and reduce direct traffic on NGeT (Next Generation e-Ticketing) website servers. In addition, anti-BOT Technology has been deployed which helps in mitigating malicious and suspicious attempts which on an average is mitigated to the extent of 64%. It helps in reducing malicious traffic and providing static content reducing load on the system and thus enhancing the user experience for genuine and verified users. During the last five years i.e. 2021 to 2025 and 2026 up to June, 22,676 touts have been arrested by RPF (Railway Protection Force) and legal action has been taken under the relevant provisions of the Railways Act, 1989. The details of spurious attempts denied to access the e-ticketing system during the last six months is as under: June 2026 Out of 19.12 billion requests, 12.61 billion were bots. (65.95%) May 2026 Out of 20.07 billion requests, 12.08 billion were bots. (60.18%) April 2026 Out of 17.33 billion requests, 10.64 billion were bots. (61.39%) March 2026 Out of 12.44 billion requests, 05.71 billion were bots. (45.90%) February 2026 Out of 11.01 billion requests, 05.01 billion were bots. (45.50%) January 2026 Out of 12.35 billion requests, 07.26 billion were bots. (58.78%) Average for last six months: Out of 15.38 billion requests, 8.88 billion were bots(57.74%). The comparative data of online and counter ticket sales during the last one year (from June 2025 to June 2026) after enforcement of strict measures in online ticket booking is as under: Online ticketing 57.90 Cr. 89% Counter booking 07.18 Cr. 11% Total 65.08 Cr. 100% This information was provided by the Union Minister for Railways, Information & Broadcasting and Electronics & Information Technology, Shri Ashwini Vaishnaw, in a reply to questions in the Lok Sabha today. ***** Dharmendra Tewari/ Dr. Nayan Solanki/ Ritu Raj/ Manik Sharma (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2287719) आगंतुक पटल  : 209 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: Urdu , हिन्दी , Gujarati Ministry of Railways RailOne App Gains Widespread Popularity Among Passengers with 4.55 Crore Downloads and Average Daily Ticket Bookings of 9.65 Lakh Indian Railways Strengthens Anti-Fraud Measures; Over 6.68 Crore User Accounts Deactivated For Unusual Mobile Numbers, Email Domains, IP Addresses Since January 2024 530 Suspicious Booking Complaints Lodged on the National Cyber Crime Portal and 13,343 Suspicious Email Domains Blocked in the year 2025-26 & 2026-27 (till 30.06.2026) 89% of Reserved Tickets Booked Online in Indian Railways Out of 65.08 Crore Tickets Booked During June 2025–June 2026; 11% Booked Through Counters प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: FASTAG BASED TOLL COLLECTION AND DIGITAL TOLLING SYSTEM
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Road Transport & Highways FASTAG BASED TOLL COLLECTION AND DIGITAL TOLLING SYSTEM प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 JUL 2026 4:59PM by PIB Delhi The Government has introduced a FASTag based Annual Pass for non-commercial cars, jeeps, and vans, which has come into effect from 15 th August, 2025. Under this scheme, an Annual Pass can be activated on payment of Rs. 3,075/- for the year 2026-27 and allows travel through all National Highway/National Expressway fee plazas for one year or up to 200 fee plaza crossings, whichever is earlier. As of June, 2026, more than 77 lakh Annual Passes have been issued registering 63 crore transactions on National Highway Fee Plazas. Presently, around 33% of total Electronic Toll Collection (ETC) transactions done by car/jeep/van are Annual Pass Transactions. The Annual Pass scheme has improved operational efficiency and enhanced the convenience of road users. The Government through National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has established multiple grievance redressal mechanisms for addressing user fee-related issues on National Highways. Complaints can be lodged through the National Highways 24×7 Toll-Free Helpline 1033, the dedicated email falsededuction@ihmcl.com , the respective FASTag issuer bank helplines, as well as through the RajmargYatra App. These mechanisms are effective, transparent, and easily accessible to road users. Further, to ensure operational integrity and transparency in user fee collection on National Highways, the Government has implemented FASTag-based electronic toll collection system. Presently, approximately more than 98% of user fee collection takes place through FASTag under National Electronic Toll Collection (NETC) program. All the FASTag transactions are processed in a secure ecosystem involving Toll Management System Software, Acquirer Bank at fee plaza, National Payment Corporation of India (NPCI) as Central Clearing House (CCH) and FASTag Issuer Bank. The transaction involves a transparent process wherein the deducted user fee (Toll) is informed to the highway users and recorded in a central repository. The Electronic Toll Collection (ETC) system is designed as such that no FASTag transaction can take place without the participation of all three stakeholders i.e., Acquirer Bank at user fee plaza, NPCI and Issuer Bank. The Apex Committee and High-Level Empowered Committee consisting of Experts from Industry and Academia, in view of security and privacy considerations, breach and overall operational control, have recommended further deliberations for GPS-based barrier-free tolling system. However, in an effort to enhance toll operations and enable seamless movement of vehicles, the Government has decided to implement MLFF through Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) with AI analytics and RFID-based Electronic Toll Collection (FASTag) which facilitates barrier-less tolling, where the user fee shall be charged from the vehicle users without having to stop, slow down or stay in a given lane. Multi-Lane Free Flow based barrier less tolling using existing FASTag (RFID)+ANPR/AI- Technology has been awarded on 17 fee plazas as per Annexure A. Out of 17 awarded fee plazas, 05 fee plazas have already gone Live i.e., Choryasi Fee Plaza (Surat, Gujarat); Mundka Fee Plaza (Delhi); Gharaunda Fee Plaza (Haryana); Manoharpura Fee Plaza (Rajasthan); Daulatpura Fee Plaza (Rajasthan). title: NHAI Strengthens Framework for Engaging Professionals in National Highway Consultancy Contracts
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Road Transport & Highways NHAI Strengthens Framework for Engaging Professionals in National Highway Consultancy Contracts Revises Consultancy RFP Provisions to Attract Experienced Engineering Professionals and Young Talent in National Highway Projects प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 JUL 2026 4:41PM by PIB Delhi With the objective of strengthening technical supervision of National Highway projects, NHAI has made amendments to the Standard Request for Proposal (RFP) documents for deployment of Authority Engineer (AE) and Independent Engineer (IE) consultancy services, mandating minimum remuneration to be paid by the Consultancy Firms to Key Professional, Sub-Professional (Civil Engineer) and Young Professional (Civil Engineer) in future contracts. Minimum monthly remuneration of Rs. 5.00 Lakhs has been fixed for Team Leader and Bridge/Structural Engineer, Rs. 2.50 Lakhs for Road Safety Expert and Rs. 3.50 Lakhs for Resident cum Highway Engineer, Program Schedule Reviewer, Senior Quality cum Material Expert and Senior Pavement Specialist. In addition to this, minimum monthly remuneration of Rs. 1.50 Lakhs for Sub-Professional (Civil Engineer) and Rs. 1.00 Lakhs for Young Professional (Civil Engineer) has been fixed. Payment of minimum mandated remuneration to the consultancy staff will be ensured through escrow arrangement. Further to create structured career progression opportunities for experienced Site Engineers, NHAI has revised the policy governing engagement of Site Engineers, which limited their tenure to a maximum of five years. To ensure that these trained professionals continue to contribute to the development of the National Highway network, NHAI has incorporated specific provisions in the General Conditions of Contract (GCC) of the AE/IE consultancy RFPs. Under the revised framework, a minimum of 20 per cent of the Sub-Professional Engineering Staff deployed by Authority Engineer and Independent Engineer consultancy firms shall comprise previously engaged Site Engineers or Young Professionals from NHAI, MoRTH or NHIDCL. The framework seeks to leverage the experience gained by these professionals in National Highway planning, construction supervision and project management, while simultaneously providing them with meaningful employment opportunities within the Highway infrastructure sector. To further promote fair and competitive compensation, NHAI has also prescribed that professionals such as Site Engineers and Young Professionals with five years or more of relevant experience shall receive a minimum monthly remuneration of Rs. 1.50 lakhs. To ensure the deployment of technically qualified, experienced and competent Key Professionals, NHAI has also introduced mandatory empanelment and interview requirements through the NHAI Skill Bridge portal. These provisions have been incorporated into the Consultancy Contract Agreements to strengthen the selection process and enhance the quality of professional engagement in National Highway consultancy assignments. These reforms represent a significant step towards institutionalizing a sustainable career pathway for engineering professionals associated with National Highway development. The revised provisions will also strengthen technical capabilities of consultancy firms engaged in National Highway development by ensuring greater participation of professionals with hands-on experience in execution and supervision of National Highway projects. This, in turn, will contribute to improved project delivery, enhanced quality standards and greater operational efficiency across the National Highway framework. By creating opportunities for experienced field engineers to transition into consultancy roles, NHAI seeks to preserve valuable technical knowledge within the sector while enhancing the quality and continuity of project supervision. NHAI remains committed to adopt progressive policy measures that promote professional excellence, attract & retain high-quality engineering talent and build institutional capacity for developing a world-class National Highway network. *** GDH/DS/HJ (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2287741) आगंतुक पटल  : 122 इस विज्ञप्ति को इन भाषाओं में पढ़ें: हिन्दी , Telugu Ministry of Road Transport & Highways NHAI Strengthens Framework for Engaging Professionals in National Highway Consultancy Contracts Revises Consultancy RFP Provisions to Attract Experienced Engineering Professionals and Young Talent in National Highway Projects प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: Dr. Jitendra Singh Informs Parliament that Over 3.75 Lakh Students and Researchers Have Benefited Under INSPIRE Programme in the Last Five Years
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Science & Technology Dr. Jitendra Singh Informs Parliament that Over 3.75 Lakh Students and Researchers Have Benefited Under INSPIRE Programme in the Last Five Years Government Strengthens INSPIRE Programme to Nurture Scientific Talent from School to Research Careers: Dr. Jitendra Singh INSPIRE Expands Outreach in Rural and Aspirational Districts, over 49,800 Students Supported Under MANAK in 2025-26 INSPIRE Programme Continues to Promote Innovation and Scientific Research Among Young Minds: Dr. Jitendra Singh प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 JUL 2026 7:19PM by PIB Delhi The Government has reaffirmed its commitment to nurturing scientific talent through the Department of Science and Technology's (DST) flagship Innovation in Science Pursuit for Inspired Research (INSPIRE) Programme, which has supported more than 3.75 lakh students and young researchers across its four major components during the last five years. The information was shared by Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Science and Technology, Dr. Jitendra Singh, in a written reply in the Lok Sabha today. Dr. Jitendra Singh informed that the INSPIRE Programme has been systematically nurturing scientific talent at different stages of the academic and research pipeline through four major components INSPIRE MANAK, INSPIRE Scholarship for Higher Education (SHE), INSPIRE Fellowship, and INSPIRE Faculty Fellowship. Together, these initiatives encourage innovation among school students, support meritorious students pursuing higher education in basic sciences, promote doctoral research, and provide opportunities for outstanding postdoctoral researchers to establish independent research careers. The Minister said INSPIRE-MANAK promotes scientific creativity among students of Classes VI to XII by encouraging original ideas and innovations. INSPIRE-SHE awards 12,000 scholarships every year, each valued at 80,000, to meritorious students pursuing undergraduate and postgraduate studies in natural and basic sciences. INSPIRE Fellowship provides financial support for doctoral research for up to five years, while the INSPIRE Faculty Fellowship enables outstanding postdoctoral researchers to undertake independent research with fellowship support and research grants. title: Government Promotes Re-Employment Opportunities For Senior Citizens Through National Career Service (NCS) Portal
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment Government Promotes Re-Employment Opportunities For Senior Citizens Through National Career Service (NCS) Portal Population Of Persons Aged 60 Years And Above Expected To Increase To 20.8 Per Cent By 2050, To Further Reach 36 Per Cent By The End Of The Century: Union Minister For Social Justice And Empowerment Dr Virendra Kumar NCS Portal Hosts 1.68 Lakh Suitable Vacancies For Senior Citizen Candidates, 1.89 Lakh Senior Citizen Job Seekers Registered On NCS Portal प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                22 JUL 2026 7:46PM by PIB Delhi The Central Government has reaffirmed its commitment to promote active ageing and enhancing employment opportunities for senior citizens through the National Career Service (NCS) Portal . The dedicated Senior Citizen Re-employment Initiative has witnessed significant growth in registrations, employer participation and job opportunities, enabling experienced professionals to continue contributing to the nation's workforce. This information was given by Union Minister for Social Justice and Empowerment Dr. Virendra Kumar in Rajya Sabha while replying to the question by Member of the House Shri Rajinder Gupta. The Minister informed the House that the Government has taken note of the findings of the UNFPA-India's India Ageing Report 2023 , which projects a significant rise in the country's elderly population. He said the report suggests that the population of persons aged 60 years and above is expected to increase from 10.4 per cent in 2022 to 20.8 per cent by 2050 , and further reach 36 per cent by the end of the century . Dr Kumar added that the report also highlights the need for policies that ensure livelihood opportunities and structured re-employment avenues to provide income security for elderly persons, particularly those working in the unorganised sector. The Minister further informed that under the NCS project, the Government has approved 407 Model Career Centres (MCCs) in collaboration with States and institutions. These centres connect youth and other job seekers, including senior citizens with employment opportunities through job fairs, the NCS Portal, career counselling and training. Dr Kumar stated that the National Career Service is playing a pivotal role in supporting India's vision of a skilled, employable and future-ready workforce adding that the platform evolving through AI-driven services, greater convergence and enhanced citizen-centric offerings, is expected to strengthen the country's modern employment services framework and contribute to inclusive economic growth and employment generation. The Minister said that since the inception of the NCS Portal in 2015 , more than 6.46 crore job seekers and 58.76 lakh employers have registered on the portal, including 1.89 lakh job seekers above the age of 60 years . Pertinently, the portal currently hosts 1.68 lakh vacancies identified as suitable for candidates above the age of 60 years. In addition, more than 2.29 crore job seekers, including senior citizens, have been shortlisted by employers through the portal across the country. *** PR-026-TAR/KV/GA (रिलीज़ आईडी: 2287971) आगंतुक पटल  : 48 Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment Government Promotes Re-Employment Opportunities For Senior Citizens Through National Career Service (NCS) Portal Population Of Persons Aged 60 Years And Above Expected To Increase To 20.8 Per Cent By 2050, To Further Reach 36 Per Cent By The End Of The Century: Union Minister For Social Justice And Empowerment Dr Virendra Kumar NCS Portal Hosts 1.68 Lakh Suitable Vacancies For Senior Citizen Candidates, 1.89 Lakh Senior Citizen Job Seekers Registered On NCS Portal प्रविष्टि तिथि:

title: WELFARE OF SENIOR CITIZENS AND PWDS IN NORTH EASTERN STATES
content:
Press Release Page | Press Information Bureau Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment WELFARE OF SENIOR CITIZENS AND PWDS IN NORTH EASTERN STATES Posted On:
                22 JUL 2026 6:15PM by PIB Delhi The Department of Social Justice and Empowerment under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment is implementing an umbrella scheme Atal Vayo Abhyudaya Yojana (AVYAY) for the welfare of the senior citizens across the country including the state of Assam and the North Eastern States. Component-wise details are given at Annexure I . The details of schemes being implemented by the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment for the welfare of persons with disabilities are given at Annexure II . Artificial Limbs Manufacturing Corporation (ALIMCO), a Public Sector Undertaking under the Department for Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities runs the Pradha Mantri Divyasha-Vayoshri Kendra (PMDVKs) for the welfare of senior citizens and persons with disabilities. At present, ALIMCO has opened 11 Pradhan Mantri Divyasha-Vayoshri Kendra (PMDVKs) in the Northeast region. ALMICO assesses the need for the opening of new centres from time to time and accordingly takes action. Annexure I Atal Vayo Abhyuday Yojana (AVYAY) has following components: - Integrated Programme for Senior Citizens (IPSrC) - Grant in aid is provided to Non-Governmental/ Voluntary Organizations for running and maintenance of senior citizen homes (old age homes), continuous care homes, etc. Facilities like shelter, nutrition, Medicare and entertainments are provided free of cost to indigent senior citizens. State Action Plan for Senior Citizens (SAPSrC) - Under State Action Plan for Senior Citizens (SAPSrC), the Government perceives a major and critical role of all State Governments in partnering and implementing the Action Plan for welfare of senior citizens. Grant in aid is provided to States/ UTs for activities like awareness generation, sensitization, cataract surgeries and State specific activities. Elderline - A National Helpline for Senior Citizens (NHSC) is a toll- free number (14567) operating for 12 hours a day (8:00 AM to 8:00 PM) that provides free Information, Guidance, Emotional Support and Field Intervention in cases of abuse and rescues in order to improve the quality of life of senior citizens. This helpline was dedicated to the Nation on 01.10.2021 by the Vice President of India. As per the Scheme Guidelines, the National Institute of Social Defense (NISD) is the Central Nodal Agency (CNA) for Elder Line. No separate state-wise allocations are made under Elderline. RashtriyaVayoshreeYojana (RVY) - ‘RashtriyaVayoshriYojana (RVY)’ objective is to provide senior citizens, belonging to BPL category or the senior citizen with the monthly income not more than Rs. 15,000/- and suffering from age related disabilities/ infirmities, with such physical aids and assisted living devices which can restore near normalcy in their bodily functions. The scheme was launched on 01.04.2017. The Scheme is implemented through the ‘Artificial Limbs Manufacturing Corporation (ALIMCO)’, (a Central Public Sector Enterprise) as the sole implementing Agency. Senior care Ageing Growth Engine (SAGE) - SAGE objective is to promote out-of-the-box and innovative solutions for the commonly faced problems, innovative start-ups would be identified and encouraged for developing products, processes and services for the welfare of the elderly. Training of Geriatric Care Givers - The main objective is to bridge the gap in supply and increasing demand in the field of geriatric caregivers so as to provide more professional services to the senior citizens and also to create a cadre of professional care givers in the field of geriatrics. National Institute of Social Defense (NISD) is the implementing agency for the scheme component. Other Initiatives for Senior Citizens: In order to solve the problems of healthy and productive ageing, several initiatives are being done across the country. The proposed initiatives are aimed at involving the elders in building up knowledge which can be useful for the society as a whole . No separate State-wise allocations are made under this component. Annexure II The Department is implementing the Scheme of ‘Assistance to Persons with Disabilities for Purchase/Fitting of Aids /Appliances (ADIP)’which includes eligible senior citizens also. Under this scheme, funds are released to various Implementing Agencies for providing aids & assistive devices to the eligible persons with disabilities (PwDs) across the country. Further, the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (DEPwD) is implementing the Awareness Generation &Publicity (AGP) Scheme as a component of the Scheme for implementation of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act (SIPDA) across the country. The Scheme aims to create awareness about the rights, entitlements, welfare measures and programmes for empowerment of persons with disabilities and to sensitize Government functionaries, service providers and the general public on disability-related issues. The information in respect of the Cross Disability Early Intervention Centre (CDEIC), a sub-scheme under the SIPDA scheme, may be seen as Appendix A . DEPwD is also implementing the 'Scholarship Scheme for Students with Disabilities' on a Pan India basis, including Assam and other North Eastern States. The main objective of the scheme is to empower students with disabilities to continue their studies so that they can earn their livelihood and get a respectable place in the society as they face many obstacles related to physical, financial, psychological in continuing their studies and living a respectable life.The scheme consists of the following six components:- Pre-matric (for classes IX and X). Post-matric (for classes XI to postgraduate degree/diploma). Higher education (for undergraduate and postgraduate degree/diploma in notified institutions of excellence in education). National Fellowship (for M.Phil and Ph.D. in Indian universities). National Overseas Scholarship (for postgraduate degree/doctorate from foreign universities). Free coaching (for government recruitment examinations and entrance examinations to technical and professional courses). The National Action Plan for Skill Development of Divyangjan (NAP-Skill provides skill development opportunities to Persons with Disabilities (PwDs) in the age group of 15 to 59 years. The objective of the scheme is to enhance their skills for gainful employment and to facilitate their transition towards self-reliance and economic participation. The skill training is provided through Government and Non-Government organizations empanelled as Training Partners with the Department. Unique Disability ID (UDID) Scheme: It is a flagship initiative of the Government of India where hospitals notified by the State/UT Government has been on boarded for issuance of disability certificates and UDID cards through the centralized UDID portal ( https://swavlambancard.gov.in/ ) to the eligible applicants who have applied through the portal. Under the Deendayal Divyangjan Rehabilitation Scheme (DDRS), financial assistance is provided to voluntary organizations to make available a range of services necessary for rehabilitation of persons with disabilities, including early intervention, development of daily living skills, education and training with a view to inclusion of persons with disabilities in the mainstream of society and actualizing their potential, the thrust is on education and training programmes. Appendix-A The Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities (DEPwD) implements Cross Disability Early Intervention Centre (CDEIC) sub-scheme under the SIPDA scheme. Under the scheme, single window Cross Disability Early Intervention Centres (CDEICs) has been launched in various National Institutes (NIs) and Composite Regional Centers (CRCs) under DEPwD to give focused attention to children in the age bracket of 0-6 years. The CDEICs are equipped to provide services for screening and identification facilities for identification of risk cases and referring for appropriate rehabilitative services; therapeutic Services viz. Speech Therapy, Occupational Therapy, Physiotherapy and Parental/Peer Counseling. At present, 28 CDEICs have been approved in National Institutes and Composite Regional Centres in various States/UTs. Further, the details of schemes of the National Trust for the Welfare of Persons with Autism, Cerebral Palsy, Mental Retardation (Intellectual Disability) and Multiple Disabilities being implemented for Persons with these categories of disabilities in Assam and other North Eastern States are as under – There are 6 Disha centres in Assam and North Eastern States, as per detail given below- S No. State District Organization Name Postal Address Mobile No Email 1 Assam Dibrugarh Mrinaljyoti  Rehabilitation Centre Mrinaljyoti Rehabilitation Centre, KumudnagarDuliajan, District: Dibrugarh, State: Assam, Pin Code:786602 9954487893 mrinaljyoti@yahoo.co.in 2 Assam Jorhat PreronaPratibandhiSishuBikash Kendra Prerona _PratibandhiSishuBikash Kendra, Cinnamara, Jorhat-8 9854044474 prerona123@rediffmail.com 3 Assam Kamrup Metro ShishuSarothi Centre For Rehabilitation And Training For Multiple Disability, Off, RK Mission Rd, Birubari, Guwahati, Assam 781016 9435040607 shishusarothi[at]gmail[dot]com 4 Manipur Imphal West Handicapped Development Foundation SagolbandTeraPukhriMapal Near KebolHighschool, Imphal West - 795001, Manipur 8132097286 hdfoundationmanipur[at]gmail[dot]com 5 Manipur Churachandpur The Malsawm Initiative Run By Centre For Community Initiative Nehru Marg, Central Lamka, Churachandpur 795128, Manipur 91 9612153082 info@communityinitiative.in 6 Meghalaya East Khasi Hills Bethany Society, JyotiSroat School, Bethany Society Lady Veronica Lane, Laitumkhrah opposite Bansara Eye Care Shillong Meghalaya - 793003 8837065270 bethanyngo1981[at]gmail[dot]com learningsanctuary@bethanysociety.org Samarth (Respite Care Scheme) - The objective of Samarth scheme is to provide respite care home for orphans or abandoned, families in crisis and also for Persons with Disabilities (Divyangjan) from BPL & LIG families including destitute with at least one of the four disabilities covered under the National Trust Act. The scheme provides for creating opportunities for family members to get respite time in order to fulfil other responsibilities. Under the Scheme Samarth Centres are set up for providing group home facility for all age groups with adequate and quality care service with acceptable living standards including provision of basic medical care from professional doctors. Niramaya (Health Insurance Scheme) – The National Trust is implementing Niramaya - Health Insurance Scheme for persons with Autism, Cerebral Palsy, Intellectual Disabilities and Multiple Disabilities. Under the Scheme, there is an insurance cover of Rs.1 lakh, which covers OPD, Diagnostic Test, Therapies, Corrective Surgeries, Alternative Medicine and Transportation. There is no age bar for enrolment under the scheme, and the treatment can be taken from any authorized medical practitioner/health care center. Any person with the aforesaid conditions can avail benefit by paying a nominal fee. The enrolment/renewal fee is not charged for Divyangjan who have Legal Guardian other than natural parents. This information is given by the Minister of State for Social Justice and Empowerment, Shri Ramdas Athawale, in a written reply in the Rajya Sabha today. ***** KV/HK (Release ID: 2287873) Visitor Counter : 48 Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment WELFARE OF SENIOR CITIZENS AND PWDS IN NORTH EASTERN STATES Posted On:
